testCases.input: Where can I find info about support orgs and shelters for UM, incl. local options?
testCases.actualOutput: You can find information about support organizations and shelters for undocumented migrants (UM), including local options, on the Stichting LOS website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and for shelters: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Additionally, the Red Cross Helpful Information website provides details about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/.
context:
Q: What are relevant websites with information about / for UM? A: 
* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.

Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.

Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/

Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).

Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.

Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.

Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

LOS is more focused on shelter details, while the Red Cross provides broader support information.

testCases.name: test_case_2
testCases.input: If UM lost access to all support orgs, what new risks might they face in NL?
testCases.actualOutput: If undocumented migrants (UM) lose access to all support organizations in the Netherlands, they face increased risks of exploitation by bad employers, slum landlords, or human traffickers due to their vulnerable position and lack of rights. Without support, they have even less access to shelter, healthcare, and basic needs, making them more likely to end up in unsafe or unhealthy situations. They are also not entitled to social benefits or health insurance, so losing support further limits their ability to get help, increasing the likelihood of homelessness, health problems, and social isolation.
context:
Q: What are relevant websites with information about / for UM? A: 
* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.

Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.

Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/

Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).

Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.

Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.

Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

Their lack of legal protection and support increases their risk of being taken advantage of.

We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/

Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).

Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.

Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.

Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

testCases.input: Analyze how limited rights to social benefits and health insurance increase UM vulnerability to exploitation.
testCases.actualOutput: Limited rights to social benefits and health insurance make undocumented migrants (UM) more vulnerable to exploitation because they cannot access basic support or protection from the government. Without social benefits, they have no financial safety net, making them dependent on informal or unsafe work, where they are at risk of being exploited by bad employers or landlords. The inability to take out health insurance means they may avoid seeking medical help, leading to unsafe or unhealthy situations. This lack of rights and support makes it easier for others to take advantage of their vulnerable position.

testCases.input: Identify the criteria distinguishing stateless persons from undocumented migrants in Dutch immigration law.
testCases.actualOutput: In Dutch immigration law, **stateless persons** are individuals who are not recognized as nationals by any country under its laws, meaning they have no nationality. **Undocumented migrants**, on the other hand, are people who do not have a valid residence permit or legal right to stay in the Netherlands, regardless of whether they have a nationality. The key distinction is that stateless persons lack any nationality, while undocumented migrants may have a nationality but lack legal residence status in the Netherlands.

testCases.input: Examine the challenges faced by stateless individuals lacking any legal residency or nationality documentation.
testCases.actualOutput: Stateless individuals without legal residency or nationality documentation face significant challenges. They have no recognized legal status, which means they cannot access basic rights such as social benefits, health insurance, or legal employment. This makes them highly vulnerable to exploitation by employers, landlords, or traffickers. They are often excluded from most government assistance and shelter programs, and finding housing is extremely difficult since most shelters require a residence permit. Their lack of documentation leaves them in unsafe or unhealthy situations and makes it easy for them to get into trouble or be taken advantage of.

testCases.name: test_case_7
testCases.input: Can EU citizens ever be considered undocumented in NL, even if their visa or permit expires?
testCases.actualOutput: No, EU citizens can never be considered undocumented in the Netherlands. EU citizens do not need to apply for a residence permit to be in the Netherlands legally, so their status does not depend on a visa or permit expiring.
context:
Q: What are relevant websites with information about / for UM? A: 
* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.

Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.

Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/

Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).

Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.

Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.

Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

testCases.input: Which specific Red Cross workshops for UM cover health care, working rights, healthy habits, and first aid?
testCases.actualOutput: The Red Cross provides workshops for undocumented migrants (UM) on health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication, and first aid. These workshops are designed to inform and support UM in these key areas. For more details about the specific workshops and how to access them, visit the Red Cross website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/
context:
Q: What are relevant websites with information about / for UM? A: 
* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.

Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.

Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/

Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).

Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.

Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.

Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

testCases.name: test_case_13
testCases.input: How can UM access Red Cross food/shelter programs, considering partner org involvement and eligibility criteria?
testCases.actualOutput: Undocumented migrants (UM) can access Red Cross food and shelter programs only through referral by a partner organization. The Red Cross does not provide direct access; eligibility and admission depend on the involvement of these partners. For shelter, the Red Cross program is limited (e.g., 10 days) and requires coordination with a partner. For more information and to find local partner organizations, UM should consult the Red Cross website (https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/) or contact the WhatsApp Helpline. Always check eligibility and availability before making referrals.

testCases.name: test_case_14
testCases.input: If BBB shelters in NL doubled capacity, how would UM access and shelter rights change?
testCases.actualOutput: If BBB shelters in the Netherlands doubled their capacity, more undocumented migrants (UM) could potentially access shelter, reducing immediate housing challenges. However, access and shelter rights would not fundamentally change, as strict admission criteria (such as having a rejected asylum request and a legal perspective on a new asylum request) would still apply. People with a Dublin claim or those who do not meet the criteria would likely still be excluded. Therefore, while more UM might find shelter, the overall rights and access procedures would remain the same. Always check local criteria and contact organizations before referring someone. (Sources: context above, https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang)
context:
Q: What are relevant websites with information about / for UM? A: 
* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.

Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.

Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/

Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).

Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.

Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.

Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.

A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).

Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

Q: Where can I find more information about local shelter programs & BBB's? 
 A: You can find information about the local shelter possibilities on the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

In the following municipalities there is a shelter program for UM: 
- Eindhoven
- Utrecht

- AmsterdamWhere can I find more information about local shelter programs & BBB's? 

You can find information about the local shelter possibilities on the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

In the following municipalities there is a shelter program for UM: 
- Eindhoven
- Utrecht
- Groningen (not on HIA yet) - screening is done by Inlia https://www.inlia.nl/nl
- Amsterdam

Q: How do winter shelters function? A: There are two different types of winter shelter. You have the permanent winter shelter and the Cold Weather Regulation. The municipality can decide if they want to organize a permanent winter shelter and if this is accessible for undocumented migrants or not. They have the legal duty to organize the Cold Weather Regulation when temperatures go below 0 degrees as it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside. The Cold Weather Regulation can be opened in the period from the 1st of November until the 1st of April.
Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters. 

Large cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) coordinate the Cold Weather Regulation together. So they often open and close at the same time. 

On the *Heplful Information website (HIA)*[https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/] you can find the opening times of the Cold Weather Regulation and winter shelters per city.

Q: Where can I find information about shelters for UM? A: On Helpful Information you can find information about local shelters for UM: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Also on the website of LOS you can find information: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: Where can I find information about the medical rights of UM? 
 A: You can find information on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/gezondheidszorg

Q: Do people have the right to see a family doctor? A: Yes, people always have the right to see a family doctor. The doctor can reimburse the costs with the CAK. 
You can refer people to this website for information on how family doctors work in the Netherlands: 
* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare

Q: How do winter shelters function? A: There are two different types of winter shelter. You have the permanent winter shelter and the Cold Weather Regulation. The municipality can decide if they want to organize a permanent winter shelter and if this is accessible for undocumented migrants or not. They have the legal duty to organize the Cold Weather Regulation when temperatures go below 0 degrees as it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside. The Cold Weather Regulation can be opened in the period from the 1st of November until the 1st of April.
Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters. 

Large cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) coordinate the Cold Weather Regulation together. So they often open and close at the same time. 

On the *Heplful Information website (HIA)*[https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/] you can find the opening times of the Cold Weather Regulation and winter shelters per city.

Q: Where can I find information about shelters for UM? A: On Helpful Information you can find information about local shelters for UM: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Also on the website of LOS you can find information: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: Where can I find information about the medical rights of UM? 
 A: You can find information on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/gezondheidszorg

Q: Do people have the right to see a family doctor? A: Yes, people always have the right to see a family doctor. The doctor can reimburse the costs with the CAK. 
You can refer people to this website for information on how family doctors work in the Netherlands: 
* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare

Q: Reimbursement of medical costs. A: * Important: it is differently arranged per target group (e.g. asylum seekers, undocumented, EU migrants. You can find more information on the website of CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/ 
• People who are undocumented have the right to receive all the necessary medical aid (medisch noodzakelijke zorg). This is care that is also in the basic health insurance. The costs are reimbursed by the CAK. you can always send the following letter to someone, they can show this letter to their doctor: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf 
• Here you can see what is in the basic package: https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/Verzekerde+zorg/basispakket-zorgverzekeringswet-zvw

What services can be reimbursed:
* General practitioners and dentists (for oral care up to the age of 18) are reimbursed for 80% by the CAK if the undocumented patient cannot pay this themselves. The CAK expects the healthcare provider to first try to recover the costs from the patient without a residence permit. Asking for payment can deter migrants without a residence permit and therefore hinders treatment compliance.
* You can only refer an undocumented patient to pharmacies, hospitals, Wlz and mental health care institutions with which the CAK has a contract. The list of contracted institutions changes regularly, for a current list visit Hetcak.nl/zakelijk/verzekeringen/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen. 
* Since 2014, there has been a personal contribution of 5 euros per medicine, unless delivery via a blister/baxter is prescribed.
* Emergency care, by both contracted and non-contracted hospitals, is reimbursed for 80%.
* Obstetric care is 100% reimbursed.
* For long-term care (nursing home), AWBZ and GGZ institutions, only contracted institutions will be reimbursed for costs.
* Dental care above the age of 18 is not reimbursed, nor are medications and aids that are not covered by the basic package or care via the WMO.

Q: What are important things to keep in mind? A: • You can ask for more details, but communicate why you are asking follow up questions
• Make it clear that as the Red Cross we don’t provide medical services, we only reffer people. 
• Let them try to contact a doctor themselves, or somobody in their network. Only if they are unable to 
call themselves, you can do it. 
• It can sometimes be quicker to find a doctor if they contact the doctor of their housemate / friend. 
• In the evening / office hours; check urgency
• Check if information is clear and if they can follow up.

Q: Where can I find informational materials about healthcare in the Netherlands? A: Informational materials in multiple languages:
https://ggdghor.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Overzicht-voorlichtingsmateriaal-in-diverse-talen-versie-2024.pdf

Video's explaining the healthcare system in the Netherlands in multiple languages:
* [English](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eCKtTKwnqDs&t=15s)
* [Dutch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWGu2EDj7wk)
* [Spanish](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_xJpzV35yg)
* [Portuguese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2XNJz2h3DQ)
* [Farsi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-RZfbTDm54k)
* [French](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUIzAnkyEtE)
* [Arabic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Zy0PqoI51M)
* [Chinese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q-b5b0UnPyY)

Q: What organizations help UM to get medical care? A: It can often be difficult for UM to get access to medical care, eventhough they have the right to get it. This is because of language barriers, or because doctors don't know about the rights of UM or because they are too busy to receive them. 

Therefore, there are in all the bigger cities support organizations that can help UM with medical care directly (because voluntary doctors are working there) or getting them acces to health care because they have a network of doctors that are willing to help. You can find this information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. 

The main organization is Doctors of the World. They have health care busses or locations, and they also do a lot of lobby and providing information. They also have a national helpdesk (https://doktersvandewereld.org/need-help) that provides help with medical care for undocumented migrants, for example:
* they can help UM find a GP close to them 
* they can teach people how to make an appointment or make an appointment for them if they cannot do it themselves
* they can help people get their medical bills reimbursed
* they can provide information about the Dutch healthcare system

Doctors of the World also provide medical care, dental care and psychological help themselves, for more information and offers in different cities see HIA.

Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: • We don’t have doctors ourselves! 
• We only give referral information or try to connect somebody with a doctor
• We do not reimburse medical costs, we sometimes can reimburse travel costs. Check this with team captain or Piket.

Q: Do people have the right to see a family doctor? A: Yes, people always have the right to see a family doctor. The doctor can reimburse the costs with the CAK. 
You can refer people to this website for information on how family doctors work in the Netherlands: 
* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare

Q: Reimbursement of medical costs. A: * Important: it is differently arranged per target group (e.g. asylum seekers, undocumented, EU migrants. You can find more information on the website of CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/ 
• People who are undocumented have the right to receive all the necessary medical aid (medisch noodzakelijke zorg). This is care that is also in the basic health insurance. The costs are reimbursed by the CAK. you can always send the following letter to someone, they can show this letter to their doctor: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf 
• Here you can see what is in the basic package: https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/Verzekerde+zorg/basispakket-zorgverzekeringswet-zvw

What services can be reimbursed:
* General practitioners and dentists (for oral care up to the age of 18) are reimbursed for 80% by the CAK if the undocumented patient cannot pay this themselves. The CAK expects the healthcare provider to first try to recover the costs from the patient without a residence permit. Asking for payment can deter migrants without a residence permit and therefore hinders treatment compliance.
* You can only refer an undocumented patient to pharmacies, hospitals, Wlz and mental health care institutions with which the CAK has a contract. The list of contracted institutions changes regularly, for a current list visit Hetcak.nl/zakelijk/verzekeringen/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen. 
* Since 2014, there has been a personal contribution of 5 euros per medicine, unless delivery via a blister/baxter is prescribed.
* Emergency care, by both contracted and non-contracted hospitals, is reimbursed for 80%.
* Obstetric care is 100% reimbursed.
* For long-term care (nursing home), AWBZ and GGZ institutions, only contracted institutions will be reimbursed for costs.
* Dental care above the age of 18 is not reimbursed, nor are medications and aids that are not covered by the basic package or care via the WMO.

Q: What are important things to keep in mind? A: • You can ask for more details, but communicate why you are asking follow up questions
• Make it clear that as the Red Cross we don’t provide medical services, we only reffer people. 
• Let them try to contact a doctor themselves, or somobody in their network. Only if they are unable to 
call themselves, you can do it. 
• It can sometimes be quicker to find a doctor if they contact the doctor of their housemate / friend. 
• In the evening / office hours; check urgency
• Check if information is clear and if they can follow up.

Q: Where can I find informational materials about healthcare in the Netherlands? A: Informational materials in multiple languages:
https://ggdghor.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Overzicht-voorlichtingsmateriaal-in-diverse-talen-versie-2024.pdf

Video's explaining the healthcare system in the Netherlands in multiple languages:
* [English](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eCKtTKwnqDs&t=15s)
* [Dutch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWGu2EDj7wk)
* [Spanish](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_xJpzV35yg)
* [Portuguese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2XNJz2h3DQ)
* [Farsi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-RZfbTDm54k)
* [French](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUIzAnkyEtE)
* [Arabic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Zy0PqoI51M)
* [Chinese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q-b5b0UnPyY)

Q: What organizations help UM to get medical care? A: It can often be difficult for UM to get access to medical care, eventhough they have the right to get it. This is because of language barriers, or because doctors don't know about the rights of UM or because they are too busy to receive them. 

Therefore, there are in all the bigger cities support organizations that can help UM with medical care directly (because voluntary doctors are working there) or getting them acces to health care because they have a network of doctors that are willing to help. You can find this information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. 

The main organization is Doctors of the World. They have health care busses or locations, and they also do a lot of lobby and providing information. They also have a national helpdesk (https://doktersvandewereld.org/need-help) that provides help with medical care for undocumented migrants, for example:
* they can help UM find a GP close to them 
* they can teach people how to make an appointment or make an appointment for them if they cannot do it themselves
* they can help people get their medical bills reimbursed
* they can provide information about the Dutch healthcare system

Doctors of the World also provide medical care, dental care and psychological help themselves, for more information and offers in different cities see HIA.

Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: • We don’t have doctors ourselves! 
• We only give referral information or try to connect somebody with a doctor
• We do not reimburse medical costs, we sometimes can reimburse travel costs. Check this with team captain or Piket.

testCases.name: test_case_22
testCases.input: How do undocumented minors access emergency shelter during extreme weather in non-participating municipalities?
testCases.actualOutput: Undocumented minors can access emergency shelter during extreme weather through the Cold Weather Regulation, which municipalities are legally required to organize when temperatures drop below 0°C, even if they do not have a permanent shelter program. This regulation ensures that it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside, and undocumented migrants—including minors—must be given access. For information on where shelters are open, you can check the Helpful Information website: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/.

Q: Where can I find more information about local shelter programs & BBB's? 
 A: You can find information about the local shelter possibilities on the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

In the following municipalities there is a shelter program for UM: 
- Eindhoven
- Utrecht
- Groningen (not on HIA yet) - screening is done by Inlia https://www.inlia.nl/nl
- AmsterdamWhere can I find more information about local shelter programs & BBB's? 

You can find information about the local shelter possibilities on the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

In the following municipalities there is a shelter program for UM: 
- Eindhoven
- Utrecht
- Groningen (not on HIA yet) - screening is done by Inlia https://www.inlia.nl/nl
- Amsterdam

Q: How do winter shelters function? A: There are two different types of winter shelter. You have the permanent winter shelter and the Cold Weather Regulation. The municipality can decide if they want to organize a permanent winter shelter and if this is accessible for undocumented migrants or not. They have the legal duty to organize the Cold Weather Regulation when temperatures go below 0 degrees as it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside. The Cold Weather Regulation can be opened in the period from the 1st of November until the 1st of April.
Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters. 

Large cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) coordinate the Cold Weather Regulation together. So they often open and close at the same time. 

On the *Heplful Information website (HIA)*[https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/] you can find the opening times of the Cold Weather Regulation and winter shelters per city.

Q: Where can I find information about shelters for UM? A: On Helpful Information you can find information about local shelters for UM: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Also on the website of LOS you can find information: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: Where can I find information about the medical rights of UM? 
 A: You can find information on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/gezondheidszorg

Q: Do people have the right to see a family doctor? A: Yes, people always have the right to see a family doctor. The doctor can reimburse the costs with the CAK. 
You can refer people to this website for information on how family doctors work in the Netherlands: 
* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare

Q: Reimbursement of medical costs. A: * Important: it is differently arranged per target group (e.g. asylum seekers, undocumented, EU migrants. You can find more information on the website of CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/ 
• People who are undocumented have the right to receive all the necessary medical aid (medisch noodzakelijke zorg). This is care that is also in the basic health insurance. The costs are reimbursed by the CAK. you can always send the following letter to someone, they can show this letter to their doctor: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf 
• Here you can see what is in the basic package: https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/Verzekerde+zorg/basispakket-zorgverzekeringswet-zvw

What services can be reimbursed:
* General practitioners and dentists (for oral care up to the age of 18) are reimbursed for 80% by the CAK if the undocumented patient cannot pay this themselves. The CAK expects the healthcare provider to first try to recover the costs from the patient without a residence permit. Asking for payment can deter migrants without a residence permit and therefore hinders treatment compliance.
* You can only refer an undocumented patient to pharmacies, hospitals, Wlz and mental health care institutions with which the CAK has a contract. The list of contracted institutions changes regularly, for a current list visit Hetcak.nl/zakelijk/verzekeringen/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen. 
* Since 2014, there has been a personal contribution of 5 euros per medicine, unless delivery via a blister/baxter is prescribed.
* Emergency care, by both contracted and non-contracted hospitals, is reimbursed for 80%.
* Obstetric care is 100% reimbursed.
* For long-term care (nursing home), AWBZ and GGZ institutions, only contracted institutions will be reimbursed for costs.
* Dental care above the age of 18 is not reimbursed, nor are medications and aids that are not covered by the basic package or care via the WMO.

Q: What are important things to keep in mind? A: • You can ask for more details, but communicate why you are asking follow up questions
• Make it clear that as the Red Cross we don’t provide medical services, we only reffer people. 
• Let them try to contact a doctor themselves, or somobody in their network. Only if they are unable to 
call themselves, you can do it. 
• It can sometimes be quicker to find a doctor if they contact the doctor of their housemate / friend. 
• In the evening / office hours; check urgency
• Check if information is clear and if they can follow up.

Q: Where can I find informational materials about healthcare in the Netherlands? A: Informational materials in multiple languages:
https://ggdghor.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Overzicht-voorlichtingsmateriaal-in-diverse-talen-versie-2024.pdf

Video's explaining the healthcare system in the Netherlands in multiple languages:
* [English](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eCKtTKwnqDs&t=15s)
* [Dutch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWGu2EDj7wk)
* [Spanish](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_xJpzV35yg)
* [Portuguese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2XNJz2h3DQ)
* [Farsi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-RZfbTDm54k)
* [French](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUIzAnkyEtE)
* [Arabic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Zy0PqoI51M)
* [Chinese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q-b5b0UnPyY)

Q: What organizations help UM to get medical care? A: It can often be difficult for UM to get access to medical care, eventhough they have the right to get it. This is because of language barriers, or because doctors don't know about the rights of UM or because they are too busy to receive them. 

Therefore, there are in all the bigger cities support organizations that can help UM with medical care directly (because voluntary doctors are working there) or getting them acces to health care because they have a network of doctors that are willing to help. You can find this information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. 

The main organization is Doctors of the World. They have health care busses or locations, and they also do a lot of lobby and providing information. They also have a national helpdesk (https://doktersvandewereld.org/need-help) that provides help with medical care for undocumented migrants, for example:
* they can help UM find a GP close to them 
* they can teach people how to make an appointment or make an appointment for them if they cannot do it themselves
* they can help people get their medical bills reimbursed
* they can provide information about the Dutch healthcare system

Doctors of the World also provide medical care, dental care and psychological help themselves, for more information and offers in different cities see HIA.

Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: • We don’t have doctors ourselves! 
• We only give referral information or try to connect somebody with a doctor
• We do not reimburse medical costs, we sometimes can reimburse travel costs. Check this with team captain or Piket.

* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare

* General practitioners and dentists (for oral care up to the age of 18) are reimbursed for 80% by the CAK if the undocumented patient cannot pay this themselves. The CAK expects the healthcare provider to first try to recover the costs from the patient without a residence permit. Asking for payment can deter migrants without a residence permit and therefore hinders treatment compliance.
* You can only refer an undocumented patient to pharmacies, hospitals, Wlz and mental health care institutions with which the CAK has a contract. The list of contracted institutions changes regularly, for a current list visit Hetcak.nl/zakelijk/verzekeringen/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen. 
* Since 2014, there has been a personal contribution of 5 euros per medicine, unless delivery via a blister/baxter is prescribed.
* Emergency care, by both contracted and non-contracted hospitals, is reimbursed for 80%.
* Obstetric care is 100% reimbursed.
* For long-term care (nursing home), AWBZ and GGZ institutions, only contracted institutions will be reimbursed for costs.
* Dental care above the age of 18 is not reimbursed, nor are medications and aids that are not covered by the basic package or care via the WMO.

• Make it clear that as the Red Cross we don’t provide medical services, we only reffer people. 
• Let them try to contact a doctor themselves, or somobody in their network. Only if they are unable to 
call themselves, you can do it. 
• It can sometimes be quicker to find a doctor if they contact the doctor of their housemate / friend. 
• In the evening / office hours; check urgency
• Check if information is clear and if they can follow up.

https://ggdghor.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Overzicht-voorlichtingsmateriaal-in-diverse-talen-versie-2024.pdf

* [Dutch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWGu2EDj7wk)
* [Spanish](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_xJpzV35yg)
* [Portuguese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2XNJz2h3DQ)
* [Farsi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-RZfbTDm54k)
* [French](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUIzAnkyEtE)
* [Arabic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Zy0PqoI51M)
* [Chinese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q-b5b0UnPyY)

Q: What organizations help UM to get medical care? A: It can often be difficult for UM to get access to medical care, eventhough they have the right to get it. This is because of language barriers, or because doctors don't know about the rights of UM or because they are too busy to receive them. 

Therefore, there are in all the bigger cities support organizations that can help UM with medical care directly (because voluntary doctors are working there) or getting them acces to health care because they have a network of doctors that are willing to help. You can find this information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. 

The main organization is Doctors of the World. They have health care busses or locations, and they also do a lot of lobby and providing information. * they can teach people how to make an appointment or make an appointment for them if they cannot do it themselves
* they can help people get their medical bills reimbursed
* they can provide information about the Dutch healthcare system

Doctors of the World also provide medical care, dental care and psychological help themselves, for more information and offers in different cities see HIA.

Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: • We don’t have doctors ourselves! 
• We only give referral information or try to connect somebody with a doctor
• We do not reimburse medical costs, we sometimes can reimburse travel costs. Check this with team captain or Piket.
