testCases.input: Are undocumented migrants in NL entitled to GP consultations, and how are costs reimbursed by CAK?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes, undocumented migrants in the Netherlands are entitled to see a general practitioner (GP). The costs for medically necessary care provided by GPs are reimbursed by the CAK if the undocumented patient cannot pay themselves. The GP can claim reimbursement for 80% of the costs from the CAK. For more details, see: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/ and https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf
context:
Q: Where can I find more information about local shelter programs & BBB's? 
 A: You can find information about the local shelter possibilities on the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

In the following municipalities there is a shelter program for UM: 
- Eindhoven
- Utrecht
- Groningen (not on HIA yet) - screening is done by Inlia https://www.inlia.nl/nl
- AmsterdamWhere can I find more information about local shelter programs & BBB's? 

You can find information about the local shelter possibilities on the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

In the following municipalities there is a shelter program for UM: 
- Eindhoven
- Utrecht
- Groningen (not on HIA yet) - screening is done by Inlia https://www.inlia.nl/nl
- Amsterdam

Q: How do winter shelters function? A: There are two different types of winter shelter. You have the permanent winter shelter and the Cold Weather Regulation. The municipality can decide if they want to organize a permanent winter shelter and if this is accessible for undocumented migrants or not. They have the legal duty to organize the Cold Weather Regulation when temperatures go below 0 degrees as it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside. The Cold Weather Regulation can be opened in the period from the 1st of November until the 1st of April.
Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters. 

Large cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) coordinate the Cold Weather Regulation together. So they often open and close at the same time. 

On the *Heplful Information website (HIA)*[https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/] you can find the opening times of the Cold Weather Regulation and winter shelters per city.

Q: Where can I find information about shelters for UM? A: On Helpful Information you can find information about local shelters for UM: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Also on the website of LOS you can find information: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: Where can I find information about the medical rights of UM? 
 A: You can find information on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/gezondheidszorg

Q: Do people have the right to see a family doctor? A: Yes, people always have the right to see a family doctor. The doctor can reimburse the costs with the CAK. 
You can refer people to this website for information on how family doctors work in the Netherlands: 
* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare

Q: Reimbursement of medical costs. A: * Important: it is differently arranged per target group (e.g. asylum seekers, undocumented, EU migrants. You can find more information on the website of CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/ 
• People who are undocumented have the right to receive all the necessary medical aid (medisch noodzakelijke zorg). This is care that is also in the basic health insurance. The costs are reimbursed by the CAK. you can always send the following letter to someone, they can show this letter to their doctor: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf 
• Here you can see what is in the basic package: https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/Verzekerde+zorg/basispakket-zorgverzekeringswet-zvw

What services can be reimbursed:
* General practitioners and dentists (for oral care up to the age of 18) are reimbursed for 80% by the CAK if the undocumented patient cannot pay this themselves. The CAK expects the healthcare provider to first try to recover the costs from the patient without a residence permit. Asking for payment can deter migrants without a residence permit and therefore hinders treatment compliance.
* You can only refer an undocumented patient to pharmacies, hospitals, Wlz and mental health care institutions with which the CAK has a contract. The list of contracted institutions changes regularly, for a current list visit Hetcak.nl/zakelijk/verzekeringen/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen. 
* Since 2014, there has been a personal contribution of 5 euros per medicine, unless delivery via a blister/baxter is prescribed.
* Emergency care, by both contracted and non-contracted hospitals, is reimbursed for 80%.
* Obstetric care is 100% reimbursed.
* For long-term care (nursing home), AWBZ and GGZ institutions, only contracted institutions will be reimbursed for costs.
* Dental care above the age of 18 is not reimbursed, nor are medications and aids that are not covered by the basic package or care via the WMO.

Q: What are important things to keep in mind? A: • You can ask for more details, but communicate why you are asking follow up questions
• Make it clear that as the Red Cross we don’t provide medical services, we only reffer people. 
• Let them try to contact a doctor themselves, or somobody in their network. Only if they are unable to 
call themselves, you can do it. 
• It can sometimes be quicker to find a doctor if they contact the doctor of their housemate / friend. 
• In the evening / office hours; check urgency
• Check if information is clear and if they can follow up.

Q: Where can I find informational materials about healthcare in the Netherlands? A: Informational materials in multiple languages:
https://ggdghor.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Overzicht-voorlichtingsmateriaal-in-diverse-talen-versie-2024.pdf

Video's explaining the healthcare system in the Netherlands in multiple languages:
* [English](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eCKtTKwnqDs&t=15s)
* [Dutch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWGu2EDj7wk)
* [Spanish](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_xJpzV35yg)
* [Portuguese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2XNJz2h3DQ)
* [Farsi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-RZfbTDm54k)
* [French](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUIzAnkyEtE)
* [Arabic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Zy0PqoI51M)
* [Chinese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q-b5b0UnPyY)

Q: What organizations help UM to get medical care? A: It can often be difficult for UM to get access to medical care, eventhough they have the right to get it. This is because of language barriers, or because doctors don't know about the rights of UM or because they are too busy to receive them. 

Therefore, there are in all the bigger cities support organizations that can help UM with medical care directly (because voluntary doctors are working there) or getting them acces to health care because they have a network of doctors that are willing to help. You can find this information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. 

The main organization is Doctors of the World. They have health care busses or locations, and they also do a lot of lobby and providing information. They also have a national helpdesk (https://doktersvandewereld.org/need-help) that provides help with medical care for undocumented migrants, for example:
* they can help UM find a GP close to them 
* they can teach people how to make an appointment or make an appointment for them if they cannot do it themselves
* they can help people get their medical bills reimbursed
* they can provide information about the Dutch healthcare system

Doctors of the World also provide medical care, dental care and psychological help themselves, for more information and offers in different cities see HIA.

Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: • We don’t have doctors ourselves! 
• We only give referral information or try to connect somebody with a doctor
• We do not reimburse medical costs, we sometimes can reimburse travel costs. Check this with team captain or Piket.

testCases.input: If UM needed urgent surgery, how would reimbursement rules affect their access to care?
testCases.actualOutput: If an undocumented migrant (UM) needs urgent surgery, they have the right to receive all necessary medical care, including emergency surgery. The costs for emergency care are reimbursed for 80% by the CAK, even if the hospital is not contracted. The hospital can try to recover the remaining costs from the patient, but care cannot be refused due to inability to pay. For more details, see: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/

Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters.

testCases.name: test_case_28
testCases.input: Which basic health insurance services does CAK reimburse for undocumented pts, incl. GP, emergency, obstetrics?
testCases.actualOutput:
CAK reimburses necessary medical care for undocumented patients that is included in the basic health insurance package. This includes:

- General practitioner (GP) care (80% reimbursed if the patient cannot pay)
- Emergency care (80% reimbursed, both contracted and non-contracted hospitals)
- Obstetric care (100% reimbursed)
- Dental care for those under 18 (80% reimbursed)
- Medicines (with a €5 personal contribution per medicine, unless prescribed via blister/baxter)
- Care from contracted pharmacies, hospitals, long-term care (nursing home), and mental health institutions

Dental care above 18, and medications or aids not in the basic package, are not reimbursed. For more details, see: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/

context:
Q: Where can I find more information about local shelter programs & BBB's? 
 A: You can find information about the local shelter possibilities on the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

In the following municipalities there is a shelter program for UM: 
- Eindhoven
- Utrecht
- Groningen (not on HIA yet) - screening is done by Inlia https://www.inlia.nl/nl
- AmsterdamWhere can I find more information about local shelter programs & BBB's? 

You can find information about the local shelter possibilities on the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

In the following municipalities there is a shelter program for UM: 
- Eindhoven
- Utrecht
- Groningen (not on HIA yet) - screening is done by Inlia https://www.inlia.nl/nl
- Amsterdam

Q: How do winter shelters function? A: There are two different types of winter shelter. You have the permanent winter shelter and the Cold Weather Regulation. The municipality can decide if they want to organize a permanent winter shelter and if this is accessible for undocumented migrants or not. They have the legal duty to organize the Cold Weather Regulation when temperatures go below 0 degrees as it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside. The Cold Weather Regulation can be opened in the period from the 1st of November until the 1st of April.
Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters. 

Large cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) coordinate the Cold Weather Regulation together. So they often open and close at the same time. 

On the *Heplful Information website (HIA)*[https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/] you can find the opening times of the Cold Weather Regulation and winter shelters per city.

Q: Where can I find information about shelters for UM? A: On Helpful Information you can find information about local shelters for UM: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Also on the website of LOS you can find information: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

Q: Where can I find information about the medical rights of UM? 
 A: You can find information on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/gezondheidszorg

Q: Do people have the right to see a family doctor? A: Yes, people always have the right to see a family doctor. The doctor can reimburse the costs with the CAK. 
You can refer people to this website for information on how family doctors work in the Netherlands: 
* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare

Q: Reimbursement of medical costs. A: * Important: it is differently arranged per target group (e.g. asylum seekers, undocumented, EU migrants. You can find more information on the website of CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/ 
• People who are undocumented have the right to receive all the necessary medical aid (medisch noodzakelijke zorg). This is care that is also in the basic health insurance. The costs are reimbursed by the CAK. you can always send the following letter to someone, they can show this letter to their doctor: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf 
• Here you can see what is in the basic package: https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/Verzekerde+zorg/basispakket-zorgverzekeringswet-zvw

What services can be reimbursed:
* General practitioners and dentists (for oral care up to the age of 18) are reimbursed for 80% by the CAK if the undocumented patient cannot pay this themselves. The CAK expects the healthcare provider to first try to recover the costs from the patient without a residence permit. Asking for payment can deter migrants without a residence permit and therefore hinders treatment compliance.
* You can only refer an undocumented patient to pharmacies, hospitals, Wlz and mental health care institutions with which the CAK has a contract. The list of contracted institutions changes regularly, for a current list visit Hetcak.nl/zakelijk/verzekeringen/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen. 
* Since 2014, there has been a personal contribution of 5 euros per medicine, unless delivery via a blister/baxter is prescribed.
* Emergency care, by both contracted and non-contracted hospitals, is reimbursed for 80%.
* Obstetric care is 100% reimbursed.
* For long-term care (nursing home), AWBZ and GGZ institutions, only contracted institutions will be reimbursed for costs.
* Dental care above the age of 18 is not reimbursed, nor are medications and aids that are not covered by the basic package or care via the WMO.

Q: What are important things to keep in mind? A: • You can ask for more details, but communicate why you are asking follow up questions
• Make it clear that as the Red Cross we don’t provide medical services, we only reffer people. 
• Let them try to contact a doctor themselves, or somobody in their network. Only if they are unable to 
call themselves, you can do it. 
• It can sometimes be quicker to find a doctor if they contact the doctor of their housemate / friend. 
• In the evening / office hours; check urgency
• Check if information is clear and if they can follow up.

Q: Where can I find informational materials about healthcare in the Netherlands? A: Informational materials in multiple languages:
https://ggdghor.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Overzicht-voorlichtingsmateriaal-in-diverse-talen-versie-2024.pdf

Video's explaining the healthcare system in the Netherlands in multiple languages:
* [English](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eCKtTKwnqDs&t=15s)
* [Dutch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWGu2EDj7wk)
* [Spanish](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_xJpzV35yg)
* [Portuguese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2XNJz2h3DQ)
* [Farsi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-RZfbTDm54k)
* [French](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUIzAnkyEtE)
* [Arabic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Zy0PqoI51M)
* [Chinese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q-b5b0UnPyY)

Q: What organizations help UM to get medical care? A: It can often be difficult for UM to get access to medical care, eventhough they have the right to get it. This is because of language barriers, or because doctors don't know about the rights of UM or because they are too busy to receive them. 

Therefore, there are in all the bigger cities support organizations that can help UM with medical care directly (because voluntary doctors are working there) or getting them acces to health care because they have a network of doctors that are willing to help. You can find this information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. 

The main organization is Doctors of the World. They have health care busses or locations, and they also do a lot of lobby and providing information. They also have a national helpdesk (https://doktersvandewereld.org/need-help) that provides help with medical care for undocumented migrants, for example:
* they can help UM find a GP close to them 
* they can teach people how to make an appointment or make an appointment for them if they cannot do it themselves
* they can help people get their medical bills reimbursed
* they can provide information about the Dutch healthcare system

Doctors of the World also provide medical care, dental care and psychological help themselves, for more information and offers in different cities see HIA.

Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: • We don’t have doctors ourselves! 
• We only give referral information or try to connect somebody with a doctor
• We do not reimburse medical costs, we sometimes can reimburse travel costs. Check this with team captain or Piket.

Q: How do winter shelters function? A: There are two different types of winter shelter. You have the permanent winter shelter and the Cold Weather Regulation. The municipality can decide if they want to organize a permanent winter shelter and if this is accessible for undocumented migrants or not. They have the legal duty to organize the Cold Weather Regulation when temperatures go below 0 degrees as it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside. The Cold Weather Regulation can be opened in the period from the 1st of November until the 1st of April.
Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters. 

Large cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) coordinate the Cold Weather Regulation together. So they often open and close at the same time. 

On the *Heplful Information website (HIA)*[https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/] you can find the opening times of the Cold Weather Regulation and winter shelters per city.

 A: You can find information on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/gezondheidszorg

* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare

• People who are undocumented have the right to receive all the necessary medical aid (medisch noodzakelijke zorg). This is care that is also in the basic health insurance. The costs are reimbursed by the CAK. you can always send the following letter to someone, they can show this letter to their doctor: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf 
• Here you can see what is in the basic package: https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/Verzekerde+zorg/basispakket-zorgverzekeringswet-zvw

• People who are undocumented have the right to receive all the necessary medical aid (medisch noodzakelijke zorg). This is care that is also in the basic health insurance. The costs are reimbursed by the CAK. you can always send the following letter to someone, they can show this letter to their doctor: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf 
• Here you can see what is in the basic package: https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/Verzekerde+zorg/basispakket-zorgverzekeringswet-zvw

Asking for payment can deter migrants without a residence permit and therefore hinders treatment compliance.
* You can only refer an undocumented patient to pharmacies, hospitals, Wlz and mental health care institutions with which the CAK has a contract. The list of contracted institutions changes regularly, for a current list visit Hetcak.nl/zakelijk/verzekeringen/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen. 
* Since 2014, there has been a personal contribution of 5 euros per medicine, unless delivery via a blister/baxter is prescribed.
* Emergency care, by both contracted and non-contracted hospitals, is reimbursed for 80%.
* Obstetric care is 100% reimbursed.
* For long-term care (nursing home), AWBZ and GGZ institutions, only contracted institutions will be reimbursed for costs.
* Dental care above the age of 18 is not reimbursed, nor are medications and aids that are not covered by the basic package or care via the WMO.

• Make it clear that as the Red Cross we don’t provide medical services, we only reffer people.

call themselves, you can do it.

• Check if information is clear and if they can follow up.

https://ggdghor.nl/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Overzicht-voorlichtingsmateriaal-in-diverse-talen-versie-2024.pdf

* [Dutch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TWGu2EDj7wk)
* [Spanish](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_xJpzV35yg)
* [Portuguese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2XNJz2h3DQ)
* [Farsi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-RZfbTDm54k)
* [French](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUIzAnkyEtE)
* [Arabic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Zy0PqoI51M)
* [Chinese](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q-b5b0UnPyY)

* they can provide information about the Dutch healthcare system

Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: • We don’t have doctors ourselves! 
• We only give referral information or try to connect somebody with a doctor
• We do not reimburse medical costs, we sometimes can reimburse travel costs. Check this with team captain or Piket.

testCases.input: Which Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland services exclude urgent aid, medical provision, and addiction-related support?
testCases.actualOutput: Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland excludes the following services: urgent assistance requests needing help within 24 hours, providing medicines or medical assistance, and support for clients with addiction problems or serious psychological issues.
context:
Q: What can the Red Cross Amsterdam do? A: ## Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland can help with: 
• Information provision and referral to partners
• Digital food and hygiene support (maximum 3 months)
• Transport costs (maximum 3 months)
• Guidance by Red Cross volunteers (to medical appointments, explaining the situation clearly)
• Access Emergency Request fund for (partial) reimbursement of medical devices

!! They **cannot** help with:
• Guidance by volunteers must be possible; We therefore do not support clients with addiction problems or serious psychological problems.
• Urgent assistance requests for which assistance must be provided within 24 hours,
• Providing medicines or medical assistance

**For help from Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland, send an e-mail to: heretohelp.amsterdam@rodekruis.nl**
Q: Where can I find a doctor? A: For an overview of where to find a doctor, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: What is better, sending somebody to a specialized organization or to a doctor? A: In general it is the best if people are known with a GP, because they can then visit the doctor more often. However, what is best to do, depends also on the situation of the person, and for example if somebody has a fixed address (better if they find a doctor) or somebody is on the street (better to go to a specialized organization). Often it is quicker to get somebody into contact with a specialized organization. This organization can then try to find a doctor for this person. Often they have a network of friendly doctors, who are more willing to receive people that are undocumented. 

In case somebody is in a city where there are specialized organizations, then it is good to give the PA the option to go to a huisarts (and if needed, our help to contact the huisarts) but that there are also specialized organizations that can help. 

**See below an example of a message that you can send:**
*You have the right to visit a family doctor, so you can always contact doctors close by to you. But there are also organizations that are specialized in providing medical help to people without health insurance. 
The benefits of contacting a doctor are that you can get structural help there. This is especially good if you have a fixed place where you are staying. However, sometimes it can teake a bit longer before there is a doctor that 
can receive you, because many doctors don’t take in new patients. 
The benefits of [ name organisation] is that they are specialized in helping people without health insurance. You can go there quickly to discuss your issue. But if you need structural help, they will also have to find you a doctor. Do you have a preference?*

Q: What if someone needs a doctor in a city without specialized support organization? A: It can sometimes take a long time before we can help somebody to get the help from a doctor. However this is somebodies right. Therefore we do try this, but in case it is taken too long, then we connect somebody with a 
specialized organization: 
• Check if somebody can call with a doctor, or has somebody in their network; give the address of 
doctors close by
• In case he cannot call; contact your TC to check if there is an option that we can call as the Red Cross
• Keep track of the doctors that you call in ‘conversation summery’ 
• If after 5 doctors it didn’t work, call with the specialized organization that is most close by to see if he can go there
• If we need to reimburse travel costs; check with Team Captain if we can do this. 
• You can always send them the letter with information about CAK (you can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

Q: What if someone needs urgent medical support after office hours/ during weekends? A: Ask him to call with huisartsenpost. In case he cannot do this: 
• Ask him his date of birth and to explain to you the symptoms. Tell him to stay on WA to answer 
questions from the Huisartsenpost and to pick up the phone in case he is called 
• Discuss with your TC if it is possible to call the huisartsenpost and discuss with them. Often they will ask to call in the patient, so then you can add the PA to the call. 
• In case you face difficulties; you can always call with piket to take over the case from you.

Q: I am afraid the doctor will send me away/ the doctor send me away A: Everyone in the Netherlands has the right to see a doctor., also if you don't have residence papers or health insurance. Clearly explain to PA what his/her rights are and that the doctor has to see him/her. Since they don't have health insurance, the costs are reimbursed by the CAK. Sometimes doctors don’t know about this. Therefore the Red Cross has developed a letter with information. In case somebody is scared to go to the doctor, then you can give them this letter, which they can show to the doctor. You can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf
Q: Can I go to the ermergency post at the hospital? A: Yes, and if it is an emergency they have the legal duty to help you. They can reimburse the costs for 80% at the CAK.

Q: Can I go to every hospital and where can I find the hospital? A: For all other help besides emergency care, you can best go to hospital that have a contract with the CAK. You can find here which hospitals have a contract with the CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15341

Q: Where can I go to a dentist? A: You can always visit a dentist, but for people older then 18 the costs are not reimbursed. This means you will often have to pay for yourself. Sometimes there is a free dental service once in a while, for example in bigger cities. 

For an overview of where to find a dentist, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Are there organizations that can help with dental care? A: Some health care organizations that are specialized in helping UM, can also help with dentists care. See the information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. Not all organizations want to be on HIA. For example Doctors of the World prefers not to have the information public, but they can help sometimes. So you can direct people to them when they need dental care, but good to not make any promises.

testCases.name: test_case_35
testCases.input: How do Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland services differ from those of specialized medical organizations?
testCases.actualOutput: Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland mainly provides support services such as information, digital food/hygiene support, transport costs, volunteer guidance to appointments, and help accessing emergency funds for medical devices. They do not provide direct medical care or medicines. In contrast, specialized medical organizations focus on providing direct medical help, especially to people without health insurance, and can connect individuals to doctors for ongoing care. If someone needs structural medical help, specialized organizations are better equipped, while the Red Cross offers practical and referral support.
context:
Q: What can the Red Cross Amsterdam do? A: ## Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland can help with: 
• Information provision and referral to partners
• Digital food and hygiene support (maximum 3 months)
• Transport costs (maximum 3 months)
• Guidance by Red Cross volunteers (to medical appointments, explaining the situation clearly)
• Access Emergency Request fund for (partial) reimbursement of medical devices

!! They **cannot** help with:
• Guidance by volunteers must be possible; We therefore do not support clients with addiction problems or serious psychological problems.
• Urgent assistance requests for which assistance must be provided within 24 hours,
• Providing medicines or medical assistance

**For help from Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland, send an e-mail to: heretohelp.amsterdam@rodekruis.nl**
Q: Where can I find a doctor? A: For an overview of where to find a doctor, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: What is better, sending somebody to a specialized organization or to a doctor? A: In general it is the best if people are known with a GP, because they can then visit the doctor more often. However, what is best to do, depends also on the situation of the person, and for example if somebody has a fixed address (better if they find a doctor) or somebody is on the street (better to go to a specialized organization). Often it is quicker to get somebody into contact with a specialized organization. This organization can then try to find a doctor for this person. Often they have a network of friendly doctors, who are more willing to receive people that are undocumented. 

In case somebody is in a city where there are specialized organizations, then it is good to give the PA the option to go to a huisarts (and if needed, our help to contact the huisarts) but that there are also specialized organizations that can help. 

**See below an example of a message that you can send:**
*You have the right to visit a family doctor, so you can always contact doctors close by to you. But there are also organizations that are specialized in providing medical help to people without health insurance. 
The benefits of contacting a doctor are that you can get structural help there. This is especially good if you have a fixed place where you are staying. However, sometimes it can teake a bit longer before there is a doctor that 
can receive you, because many doctors don’t take in new patients. 
The benefits of [ name organisation] is that they are specialized in helping people without health insurance. You can go there quickly to discuss your issue. But if you need structural help, they will also have to find you a doctor. Do you have a preference?*

Q: What if someone needs a doctor in a city without specialized support organization? A: It can sometimes take a long time before we can help somebody to get the help from a doctor. However this is somebodies right. Therefore we do try this, but in case it is taken too long, then we connect somebody with a 
specialized organization: 
• Check if somebody can call with a doctor, or has somebody in their network; give the address of 
doctors close by
• In case he cannot call; contact your TC to check if there is an option that we can call as the Red Cross
• Keep track of the doctors that you call in ‘conversation summery’ 
• If after 5 doctors it didn’t work, call with the specialized organization that is most close by to see if he can go there
• If we need to reimburse travel costs; check with Team Captain if we can do this. 
• You can always send them the letter with information about CAK (you can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

Q: What if someone needs urgent medical support after office hours/ during weekends? A: Ask him to call with huisartsenpost. In case he cannot do this: 
• Ask him his date of birth and to explain to you the symptoms. Tell him to stay on WA to answer 
questions from the Huisartsenpost and to pick up the phone in case he is called 
• Discuss with your TC if it is possible to call the huisartsenpost and discuss with them. Often they will ask to call in the patient, so then you can add the PA to the call. 
• In case you face difficulties; you can always call with piket to take over the case from you.

Q: I am afraid the doctor will send me away/ the doctor send me away A: Everyone in the Netherlands has the right to see a doctor., also if you don't have residence papers or health insurance. Clearly explain to PA what his/her rights are and that the doctor has to see him/her. Since they don't have health insurance, the costs are reimbursed by the CAK. Sometimes doctors don’t know about this. Therefore the Red Cross has developed a letter with information. In case somebody is scared to go to the doctor, then you can give them this letter, which they can show to the doctor. You can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf
Q: Can I go to the ermergency post at the hospital? A: Yes, and if it is an emergency they have the legal duty to help you. They can reimburse the costs for 80% at the CAK.

Q: Can I go to every hospital and where can I find the hospital? A: For all other help besides emergency care, you can best go to hospital that have a contract with the CAK. You can find here which hospitals have a contract with the CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15341

Q: Where can I go to a dentist? A: You can always visit a dentist, but for people older then 18 the costs are not reimbursed. This means you will often have to pay for yourself. Sometimes there is a free dental service once in a while, for example in bigger cities. 

For an overview of where to find a dentist, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Are there organizations that can help with dental care? A: Some health care organizations that are specialized in helping UM, can also help with dentists care. See the information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. Not all organizations want to be on HIA. For example Doctors of the World prefers not to have the information public, but they can help sometimes. So you can direct people to them when they need dental care, but good to not make any promises.

testCases.input: Identify which client situations and urgent needs Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland cannot address, explaining why.
testCases.actualOutput:
Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland cannot address the following client situations and urgent needs:

- They cannot provide guidance by volunteers to clients with addiction problems or serious psychological problems, because their volunteers are not equipped to support these cases.
- They cannot respond to urgent assistance requests that require help within 24 hours, as they are not set up for immediate crisis intervention.
- They cannot provide medicines or medical assistance, since this is outside their scope of services.

These limitations exist because the organization’s resources and expertise are focused on information provision, limited financial support, and non-medical guidance, not on urgent, medical, or highly specialized care.

• Access Emergency Request fund for (partial) reimbursement of medical devices

• Providing medicines or medical assistance

Undocumented migrants in the Netherlands have the right to see a doctor, including a GP (huisarts) and emergency care. Steps they can take:

1. **Contact a GP (huisarts):** They can visit a family doctor. If they have a fixed address, it is best to register with a GP for ongoing care. If they have trouble finding a GP, they can ask for help from organizations like the Red Cross or specialized organizations for undocumented migrants.

2. **Use specialized organizations:** In cities with specialized organizations, these can help undocumented migrants access medical care and may have networks of doctors willing to help.

3. **Emergency care:** For urgent medical needs, they can go to the emergency post at a hospital. Hospitals have a legal duty to help in emergencies, regardless of insurance or residence status.

4. **After-hours care:** For urgent issues outside office hours, they should call the huisartsenpost (out-of-hours GP service). If they cannot do this themselves, the Red Cross may assist.

5. **Bring supporting documents:** If a doctor is hesitant, migrants can show the Red Cross letter explaining their rights and the CAK reimbursement for costs: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

6. **Cost reimbursement:** Medical costs for undocumented migrants are often reimbursed by the CAK, especially for necessary care.

For more information or help, they can contact the Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland at heretohelp.amsterdam@rodekruis.nl.
context:
Q: What can the Red Cross Amsterdam do? A: ## Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland can help with: 
• Information provision and referral to partners
• Digital food and hygiene support (maximum 3 months)
• Transport costs (maximum 3 months)
• Guidance by Red Cross volunteers (to medical appointments, explaining the situation clearly)
• Access Emergency Request fund for (partial) reimbursement of medical devices

!! They **cannot** help with:
• Guidance by volunteers must be possible; We therefore do not support clients with addiction problems or serious psychological problems.
• Urgent assistance requests for which assistance must be provided within 24 hours,
• Providing medicines or medical assistance

**For help from Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland, send an e-mail to: heretohelp.amsterdam@rodekruis.nl**
Q: Where can I find a doctor? A: For an overview of where to find a doctor, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: What is better, sending somebody to a specialized organization or to a doctor? A: In general it is the best if people are known with a GP, because they can then visit the doctor more often. However, what is best to do, depends also on the situation of the person, and for example if somebody has a fixed address (better if they find a doctor) or somebody is on the street (better to go to a specialized organization). Often it is quicker to get somebody into contact with a specialized organization. This organization can then try to find a doctor for this person. Often they have a network of friendly doctors, who are more willing to receive people that are undocumented. 

In case somebody is in a city where there are specialized organizations, then it is good to give the PA the option to go to a huisarts (and if needed, our help to contact the huisarts) but that there are also specialized organizations that can help. 

**See below an example of a message that you can send:**
*You have the right to visit a family doctor, so you can always contact doctors close by to you. But there are also organizations that are specialized in providing medical help to people without health insurance. 
The benefits of contacting a doctor are that you can get structural help there. This is especially good if you have a fixed place where you are staying. However, sometimes it can teake a bit longer before there is a doctor that 
can receive you, because many doctors don’t take in new patients. 
The benefits of [ name organisation] is that they are specialized in helping people without health insurance. You can go there quickly to discuss your issue. But if you need structural help, they will also have to find you a doctor. Do you have a preference?*

Q: What if someone needs a doctor in a city without specialized support organization? A: It can sometimes take a long time before we can help somebody to get the help from a doctor. However this is somebodies right. Therefore we do try this, but in case it is taken too long, then we connect somebody with a 
specialized organization: 
• Check if somebody can call with a doctor, or has somebody in their network; give the address of 
doctors close by
• In case he cannot call; contact your TC to check if there is an option that we can call as the Red Cross
• Keep track of the doctors that you call in ‘conversation summery’ 
• If after 5 doctors it didn’t work, call with the specialized organization that is most close by to see if he can go there
• If we need to reimburse travel costs; check with Team Captain if we can do this. 
• You can always send them the letter with information about CAK (you can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

Q: What if someone needs urgent medical support after office hours/ during weekends? A: Ask him to call with huisartsenpost. In case he cannot do this: 
• Ask him his date of birth and to explain to you the symptoms. Tell him to stay on WA to answer 
questions from the Huisartsenpost and to pick up the phone in case he is called 
• Discuss with your TC if it is possible to call the huisartsenpost and discuss with them. Often they will ask to call in the patient, so then you can add the PA to the call. 
• In case you face difficulties; you can always call with piket to take over the case from you.

Q: I am afraid the doctor will send me away/ the doctor send me away A: Everyone in the Netherlands has the right to see a doctor., also if you don't have residence papers or health insurance. Clearly explain to PA what his/her rights are and that the doctor has to see him/her. Since they don't have health insurance, the costs are reimbursed by the CAK. Sometimes doctors don’t know about this. Therefore the Red Cross has developed a letter with information. In case somebody is scared to go to the doctor, then you can give them this letter, which they can show to the doctor. You can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf
Q: Can I go to the ermergency post at the hospital? A: Yes, and if it is an emergency they have the legal duty to help you. They can reimburse the costs for 80% at the CAK.

Q: Can I go to every hospital and where can I find the hospital? A: For all other help besides emergency care, you can best go to hospital that have a contract with the CAK. You can find here which hospitals have a contract with the CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15341

Q: Where can I go to a dentist? A: You can always visit a dentist, but for people older then 18 the costs are not reimbursed. This means you will often have to pay for yourself. Sometimes there is a free dental service once in a while, for example in bigger cities. 

For an overview of where to find a dentist, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Are there organizations that can help with dental care? A: Some health care organizations that are specialized in helping UM, can also help with dentists care. See the information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. Not all organizations want to be on HIA. For example Doctors of the World prefers not to have the information public, but they can help sometimes. So you can direct people to them when they need dental care, but good to not make any promises.

testCases.input: What steps should be taken for urgent medical support after office hours if the patient cannot call?
testCases.actualOutput: If urgent medical support is needed after office hours and the patient cannot call, ask for their date of birth and symptoms, and tell them to stay available to answer questions from the Huisartsenpost and to pick up the phone if called. Discuss with your Team Captain (TC) if you can call the Huisartsenpost on their behalf—often, they will ask to speak directly with the patient, so you can add the patient to the call. If you face difficulties, you can always call with piket to take over the case.

testCases.input: Is emergency hospital care accessible and reimbursable for uninsured individuals, and what percentage is covered?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes, emergency hospital care is accessible for uninsured individuals in the Netherlands, and hospitals have a legal duty to help in emergencies. The costs can be reimbursed for 80% at the CAK.
context:
Q: What can the Red Cross Amsterdam do? A: ## Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland can help with: 
• Information provision and referral to partners
• Digital food and hygiene support (maximum 3 months)
• Transport costs (maximum 3 months)
• Guidance by Red Cross volunteers (to medical appointments, explaining the situation clearly)
• Access Emergency Request fund for (partial) reimbursement of medical devices

!! They **cannot** help with:
• Guidance by volunteers must be possible; We therefore do not support clients with addiction problems or serious psychological problems.
• Urgent assistance requests for which assistance must be provided within 24 hours,
• Providing medicines or medical assistance

**For help from Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland, send an e-mail to: heretohelp.amsterdam@rodekruis.nl**
Q: Where can I find a doctor? A: For an overview of where to find a doctor, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: What is better, sending somebody to a specialized organization or to a doctor? A: In general it is the best if people are known with a GP, because they can then visit the doctor more often. However, what is best to do, depends also on the situation of the person, and for example if somebody has a fixed address (better if they find a doctor) or somebody is on the street (better to go to a specialized organization). Often it is quicker to get somebody into contact with a specialized organization. This organization can then try to find a doctor for this person. Often they have a network of friendly doctors, who are more willing to receive people that are undocumented. 

In case somebody is in a city where there are specialized organizations, then it is good to give the PA the option to go to a huisarts (and if needed, our help to contact the huisarts) but that there are also specialized organizations that can help. 

**See below an example of a message that you can send:**
*You have the right to visit a family doctor, so you can always contact doctors close by to you. But there are also organizations that are specialized in providing medical help to people without health insurance. 
The benefits of contacting a doctor are that you can get structural help there. This is especially good if you have a fixed place where you are staying. However, sometimes it can teake a bit longer before there is a doctor that 
can receive you, because many doctors don’t take in new patients. 
The benefits of [ name organisation] is that they are specialized in helping people without health insurance. You can go there quickly to discuss your issue. But if you need structural help, they will also have to find you a doctor. Do you have a preference?*

Q: What if someone needs a doctor in a city without specialized support organization? A: It can sometimes take a long time before we can help somebody to get the help from a doctor. However this is somebodies right. Therefore we do try this, but in case it is taken too long, then we connect somebody with a 
specialized organization: 
• Check if somebody can call with a doctor, or has somebody in their network; give the address of 
doctors close by
• In case he cannot call; contact your TC to check if there is an option that we can call as the Red Cross
• Keep track of the doctors that you call in ‘conversation summery’ 
• If after 5 doctors it didn’t work, call with the specialized organization that is most close by to see if he can go there
• If we need to reimburse travel costs; check with Team Captain if we can do this. 
• You can always send them the letter with information about CAK (you can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

Q: What if someone needs urgent medical support after office hours/ during weekends? A: Ask him to call with huisartsenpost. In case he cannot do this: 
• Ask him his date of birth and to explain to you the symptoms. Tell him to stay on WA to answer 
questions from the Huisartsenpost and to pick up the phone in case he is called 
• Discuss with your TC if it is possible to call the huisartsenpost and discuss with them. Often they will ask to call in the patient, so then you can add the PA to the call. 
• In case you face difficulties; you can always call with piket to take over the case from you.

Clearly explain to PA what his/her rights are and that the doctor has to see him/her. Since they don't have health insurance, the costs are reimbursed by the CAK. Sometimes doctors don’t know about this. Therefore the Red Cross has developed a letter with information. In case somebody is scared to go to the doctor, then you can give them this letter, which they can show to the doctor. You can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

Q: Can I go to every hospital and where can I find the hospital? A: For all other help besides emergency care, you can best go to hospital that have a contract with the CAK. You can find here which hospitals have a contract with the CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15341

Q: Where can I go to a dentist? A: You can always visit a dentist, but for people older then 18 the costs are not reimbursed. This means you will often have to pay for yourself. Sometimes there is a free dental service once in a while, for example in bigger cities. 

For an overview of where to find a dentist, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Are there organizations that can help with dental care? A: Some health care organizations that are specialized in helping UM, can also help with dentists care. See the information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. Not all organizations want to be on HIA. For example Doctors of the World prefers not to have the information public, but they can help sometimes. So you can direct people to them when they need dental care, but good to not make any promises.

testCases.input: How do hospitals with CAK contracts differ from other hospitals in treating uninsured patients?
testCases.actualOutput: Hospitals with CAK contracts are specifically set up to provide care to uninsured patients, as they can directly claim reimbursement for most treatments through the CAK. This makes it easier for uninsured patients to access non-emergency care at these hospitals. Other hospitals may not have this arrangement, so it is best for uninsured patients to go to hospitals with a CAK contract for non-emergency care. For emergencies, all hospitals are legally required to provide help.

testCases.name: test_case_51
testCases.input: How do shelter options differ for undocumented pregnant women before and after childbirth?
testCases.actualOutput: Undocumented pregnant women have the right to shelter for 6 weeks before the birth and 6 weeks after the birth. This means shelter is specifically available during this 12-week period surrounding childbirth. Before the 6 weeks prior to birth and after the 6 weeks following birth, there is no guaranteed right to shelter mentioned in the context.
context:
Q: Where can I go when I am pregnant? A: People who are undocumented have the right to see a midwife after they are pregnant for three months. Women who are pregnant also have the right to get shelter for the period of 6 weeks before the birth and 6 weeks after the birth. For a midwife, somebody doesn’t have to first see a doctor. So they can contact a midwife directly.

For an overview of where to go when you are pregnant, please see HIA (Pregnancy & Sexual Health): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

For more information about pregnancy in 13 different languages, see:
https://www.zanzu.de/nl/gezinsplanning-en-zwangerschap/

Q: Where can I go when I want to get an abortion? A: If your pregnancy wasn’t planned and you’re considering your options, abortion is a possibility. How abortion can be carried out depends on how far you are in the pregnancy. The costs are usually not reimbursed but there are options for you if you are unable to pay for it yourself. Please check HIA for more information (women) - https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Where can I go for physiotherapy? A: Since physiotherapy is in not in the basic health insurence, it is not compensated. This means somebody has to pay for it themselves. Somethimes special organizations can help. 

For an overview of where to find a physiotherapist and which special organizations can help with payment, please see HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Where can I go for information about or help with HIV, STD and birth control? A: For an overview of where to go to get more information or help with HIV, STD or birthcontrol, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

For more information about relationships, sexual health and pregnancy in 13 languages, see: https://www.zanzu.nl/nl/taalkeuze

Q: Where can I get medication? A: In case a PA needs medicine, they need a recipe from the doctor. So first check if the person has this. In case the person has a prescription, they can go to a pharmacy that has a contract with the CAK. They have to pay €5,- for the medicine.

Check which pharmacies are contracted with the CAK. You can find the list here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340 

Please see HIA for an overview of the listed pharmacies per city: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ (health & wellbeing - medication)

Q: How can I get a repeat prescription? A: If somebody needs a repeat prescription, but doesn’t have the prescription anymore or used to get it in their home country, it can help to contact a contracted pharmacy directly to discuss this with them. Maybe they are willing to give it or they know a doctor where this person can go to. 

You can find the list of pharmacies contracted with the CAK here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340

Q: Where can I go to for psychosocial support? A: For an overview of where to go for psychosocial support, please see HIA (Mental Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

In addition, you can send them this folder about mental wellbeing (it's available in multiple languages): https://www.pharos.nl/kennisbank/als-je-stress-hebt-veel-denkt-en-slecht-slaapt-engels/

**IMPORTANT** In general when somebody is saying that he feels depressed, it is important that the PA receives good help from us. It can be important that they are helped by only one person and don’t get answers from different helpdesk agents. When you have the feeling that somebody is not feeling well, inform the Team Captain or piket about it, to see if she should take over the case.

Q: Do people have the right to get legal assistance? A: Everyone has the right to legal assistance, including people without a residence permit. A Juridisch Loket (legal help desk) can help with legal issues. Some cities have legal aid centres that provide assistance. Other relief organisations, such as VluchtelingenWerk (the Dutch Refugee Council), ASKV Refugee Support and Stek, also help people without residence permits.

Q: Where can somebody go if they want to request asylum for the first time? A: People that are looking for asylum can best go to VluchtelingenWerk for advice. VluchtelingenWerk also has a 
website where people can get information or get into contact with VluchtelingenWerk: www.refugeehelp.nl

Q: Who can help someone who has been rejected for asylum, but wants to try it again? A: People that have a negative decision on their asylum, might be able to get juridical help and in some cases temporary shelter. It is good to check with them what kind of help they already received, and where they are staying. In most cities there are organizations that can give juridical advice to people that are undocumented (and received a negative decision).
You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. In case there is no specialized organization close by, then it is best to send them to VluchtelingenWerk.

testCases.name: test_case_60
testCases.input: How do options for finding physiotherapists and payment help differ from other health services?
testCases.actualOutput: Options for finding physiotherapists and payment help differ from other health services because physiotherapy is not included in the basic health insurance and is not compensated, so individuals must pay for it themselves. In some cases, special organizations can help with payment. For other health services like seeing a midwife, getting medication, or psychosocial support, there are rights to access and sometimes partial coverage or support, especially for undocumented people. For physiotherapy, you need to check HIA for where to find a physiotherapist and which organizations might help with payment: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
context:
Q: Where can I go when I am pregnant? A: People who are undocumented have the right to see a midwife after they are pregnant for three months. Women who are pregnant also have the right to get shelter for the period of 6 weeks before the birth and 6 weeks after the birth. For a midwife, somebody doesn’t have to first see a doctor. So they can contact a midwife directly.

For an overview of where to go when you are pregnant, please see HIA (Pregnancy & Sexual Health): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

For more information about pregnancy in 13 different languages, see:
https://www.zanzu.de/nl/gezinsplanning-en-zwangerschap/

Q: Where can I go when I want to get an abortion? A: If your pregnancy wasn’t planned and you’re considering your options, abortion is a possibility. How abortion can be carried out depends on how far you are in the pregnancy. The costs are usually not reimbursed but there are options for you if you are unable to pay for it yourself. Please check HIA for more information (women) - https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Where can I go for physiotherapy? A: Since physiotherapy is in not in the basic health insurence, it is not compensated. This means somebody has to pay for it themselves. Somethimes special organizations can help. 

For an overview of where to find a physiotherapist and which special organizations can help with payment, please see HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Where can I go for information about or help with HIV, STD and birth control? A: For an overview of where to go to get more information or help with HIV, STD or birthcontrol, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

For more information about relationships, sexual health and pregnancy in 13 languages, see: https://www.zanzu.nl/nl/taalkeuze

Q: Where can I get medication? A: In case a PA needs medicine, they need a recipe from the doctor. So first check if the person has this. In case the person has a prescription, they can go to a pharmacy that has a contract with the CAK. They have to pay €5,- for the medicine.

Check which pharmacies are contracted with the CAK. You can find the list here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340 

Please see HIA for an overview of the listed pharmacies per city: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ (health & wellbeing - medication)

Q: How can I get a repeat prescription? A: If somebody needs a repeat prescription, but doesn’t have the prescription anymore or used to get it in their home country, it can help to contact a contracted pharmacy directly to discuss this with them. Maybe they are willing to give it or they know a doctor where this person can go to. 

You can find the list of pharmacies contracted with the CAK here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340

Q: Where can I go to for psychosocial support? A: For an overview of where to go for psychosocial support, please see HIA (Mental Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

In addition, you can send them this folder about mental wellbeing (it's available in multiple languages): https://www.pharos.nl/kennisbank/als-je-stress-hebt-veel-denkt-en-slecht-slaapt-engels/

**IMPORTANT** In general when somebody is saying that he feels depressed, it is important that the PA receives good help from us. It can be important that they are helped by only one person and don’t get answers from different helpdesk agents. When you have the feeling that somebody is not feeling well, inform the Team Captain or piket about it, to see if she should take over the case.

Q: Do people have the right to get legal assistance? A: Everyone has the right to legal assistance, including people without a residence permit. A Juridisch Loket (legal help desk) can help with legal issues. Some cities have legal aid centres that provide assistance. Other relief organisations, such as VluchtelingenWerk (the Dutch Refugee Council), ASKV Refugee Support and Stek, also help people without residence permits.

Q: Where can somebody go if they want to request asylum for the first time? A: People that are looking for asylum can best go to VluchtelingenWerk for advice. VluchtelingenWerk also has a 
website where people can get information or get into contact with VluchtelingenWerk: www.refugeehelp.nl

Q: Who can help someone who has been rejected for asylum, but wants to try it again? A: People that have a negative decision on their asylum, might be able to get juridical help and in some cases temporary shelter. It is good to check with them what kind of help they already received, and where they are staying. In most cities there are organizations that can give juridical advice to people that are undocumented (and received a negative decision).
You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. In case there is no specialized organization close by, then it is best to send them to VluchtelingenWerk.

testCases.name: test_case_62
testCases.input: Suppose you move to NL and need info on sexual health in Turkish. Where could you look?
testCases.actualOutput: You can find information about sexual health in Turkish at https://www.zanzu.nl/nl/taalkeuze, where resources are available in 13 different languages, including Turkish.
context:
Q: Where can I go when I am pregnant? A: People who are undocumented have the right to see a midwife after they are pregnant for three months. Women who are pregnant also have the right to get shelter for the period of 6 weeks before the birth and 6 weeks after the birth. For a midwife, somebody doesn’t have to first see a doctor. So they can contact a midwife directly.

For an overview of where to go when you are pregnant, please see HIA (Pregnancy & Sexual Health): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

For more information about pregnancy in 13 different languages, see:
https://www.zanzu.de/nl/gezinsplanning-en-zwangerschap/

Q: Where can I go when I want to get an abortion? A: If your pregnancy wasn’t planned and you’re considering your options, abortion is a possibility. How abortion can be carried out depends on how far you are in the pregnancy. The costs are usually not reimbursed but there are options for you if you are unable to pay for it yourself. Please check HIA for more information (women) - https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Where can I go for physiotherapy? A: Since physiotherapy is in not in the basic health insurence, it is not compensated. This means somebody has to pay for it themselves. Somethimes special organizations can help. 

For an overview of where to find a physiotherapist and which special organizations can help with payment, please see HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Where can I go for information about or help with HIV, STD and birth control? A: For an overview of where to go to get more information or help with HIV, STD or birthcontrol, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

For more information about relationships, sexual health and pregnancy in 13 languages, see: https://www.zanzu.nl/nl/taalkeuze

Q: Where can I get medication? A: In case a PA needs medicine, they need a recipe from the doctor. So first check if the person has this. In case the person has a prescription, they can go to a pharmacy that has a contract with the CAK. They have to pay €5,- for the medicine.

Check which pharmacies are contracted with the CAK. You can find the list here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340 

Please see HIA for an overview of the listed pharmacies per city: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ (health & wellbeing - medication)

Q: How can I get a repeat prescription? A: If somebody needs a repeat prescription, but doesn’t have the prescription anymore or used to get it in their home country, it can help to contact a contracted pharmacy directly to discuss this with them. Maybe they are willing to give it or they know a doctor where this person can go to. 

You can find the list of pharmacies contracted with the CAK here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340

Q: Where can I go to for psychosocial support? A: For an overview of where to go for psychosocial support, please see HIA (Mental Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

In addition, you can send them this folder about mental wellbeing (it's available in multiple languages): https://www.pharos.nl/kennisbank/als-je-stress-hebt-veel-denkt-en-slecht-slaapt-engels/

**IMPORTANT** In general when somebody is saying that he feels depressed, it is important that the PA receives good help from us. It can be important that they are helped by only one person and don’t get answers from different helpdesk agents. When you have the feeling that somebody is not feeling well, inform the Team Captain or piket about it, to see if she should take over the case.

Q: Do people have the right to get legal assistance? A: Everyone has the right to legal assistance, including people without a residence permit. A Juridisch Loket (legal help desk) can help with legal issues. Some cities have legal aid centres that provide assistance. Other relief organisations, such as VluchtelingenWerk (the Dutch Refugee Council), ASKV Refugee Support and Stek, also help people without residence permits.

Q: Where can somebody go if they want to request asylum for the first time? A: People that are looking for asylum can best go to VluchtelingenWerk for advice. VluchtelingenWerk also has a 
website where people can get information or get into contact with VluchtelingenWerk: www.refugeehelp.nl

Q: Who can help someone who has been rejected for asylum, but wants to try it again? A: People that have a negative decision on their asylum, might be able to get juridical help and in some cases temporary shelter. It is good to check with them what kind of help they already received, and where they are staying. In most cities there are organizations that can give juridical advice to people that are undocumented (and received a negative decision).
You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. In case there is no specialized organization close by, then it is best to send them to VluchtelingenWerk.

Q: Where can I go when I am pregnant? A: People who are undocumented have the right to see a midwife after they are pregnant for three months. Women who are pregnant also have the right to get shelter for the period of 6 weeks before the birth and 6 weeks after the birth. For a midwife, somebody doesn’t have to first see a doctor. So they can contact a midwife directly.

For an overview of where to go when you are pregnant, please see HIA (Pregnancy & Sexual Health): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

For more information about pregnancy in 13 different languages, see:
https://www.zanzu.de/nl/gezinsplanning-en-zwangerschap/

Q: Where can I go when I want to get an abortion? A: If your pregnancy wasn’t planned and you’re considering your options, abortion is a possibility. How abortion can be carried out depends on how far you are in the pregnancy. The costs are usually not reimbursed but there are options for you if you are unable to pay for it yourself. Please check HIA for more information (women) - https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Where can I go for physiotherapy? A: Since physiotherapy is in not in the basic health insurence, it is not compensated. This means somebody has to pay for it themselves. Somethimes special organizations can help. 

For an overview of where to find a physiotherapist and which special organizations can help with payment, please see HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Q: Where can I go for information about or help with HIV, STD and birth control? A: For an overview of where to go to get more information or help with HIV, STD or birthcontrol, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

For more information about relationships, sexual health and pregnancy in 13 languages, see: https://www.zanzu.nl/nl/taalkeuze

Q: Where can I get medication? A: In case a PA needs medicine, they need a recipe from the doctor. So first check if the person has this. In case the person has a prescription, they can go to a pharmacy that has a contract with the CAK. They have to pay €5,- for the medicine.

Check which pharmacies are contracted with the CAK. You can find the list here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340 

Please see HIA for an overview of the listed pharmacies per city: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ (health & wellbeing - medication)

Q: How can I get a repeat prescription? A: If somebody needs a repeat prescription, but doesn’t have the prescription anymore or used to get it in their home country, it can help to contact a contracted pharmacy directly to discuss this with them. Maybe they are willing to give it or they know a doctor where this person can go to. 

You can find the list of pharmacies contracted with the CAK here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340

Q: Where can I go to for psychosocial support? A: For an overview of where to go for psychosocial support, please see HIA (Mental Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

In addition, you can send them this folder about mental wellbeing (it's available in multiple languages): https://www.pharos.nl/kennisbank/als-je-stress-hebt-veel-denkt-en-slecht-slaapt-engels/

**IMPORTANT** In general when somebody is saying that he feels depressed, it is important that the PA receives good help from us. It can be important that they are helped by only one person and don’t get answers from different helpdesk agents. When you have the feeling that somebody is not feeling well, inform the Team Captain or piket about it, to see if she should take over the case.

Q: Do people have the right to get legal assistance? A: Everyone has the right to legal assistance, including people without a residence permit. A Juridisch Loket (legal help desk) can help with legal issues. Some cities have legal aid centres that provide assistance. Other relief organisations, such as VluchtelingenWerk (the Dutch Refugee Council), ASKV Refugee Support and Stek, also help people without residence permits.

Q: Where can somebody go if they want to request asylum for the first time? A: People that are looking for asylum can best go to VluchtelingenWerk for advice. VluchtelingenWerk also has a 
website where people can get information or get into contact with VluchtelingenWerk: www.refugeehelp.nl

Q: Who can help someone who has been rejected for asylum, but wants to try it again? A: People that have a negative decision on their asylum, might be able to get juridical help and in some cases temporary shelter. It is good to check with them what kind of help they already received, and where they are staying. In most cities there are organizations that can give juridical advice to people that are undocumented (and received a negative decision).
You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. In case there is no specialized organization close by, then it is best to send them to VluchtelingenWerk.

testCases.name: test_case_65
testCases.input: How do CAK-contracted pharmacies for prescriptions differ from regular pharmacies in access and payment?
testCases.actualOutput: CAK-contracted pharmacies differ from regular pharmacies because they specifically serve people without health insurance, allowing them to get prescribed medication for a fixed fee of €5 per medicine. Regular pharmacies may not offer this arrangement, and costs could be higher. To use a CAK-contracted pharmacy, a prescription from a doctor is required. You can find a list of these pharmacies here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340

Q: Where can I get medication? A: In case a PA needs medicine, they need a recipe from the doctor. So first check if the person has this. In case the person has a prescription, they can go to a pharmacy that has a contract with the CAK. They have to pay €5,- for the medicine.

Check which pharmacies are contracted with the CAK. You can find the list here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340 

Please see HIA for an overview of the listed pharmacies per city: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ (health & wellbeing - medication)

Q: How can I get a repeat prescription? A: If somebody needs a repeat prescription, but doesn’t have the prescription anymore or used to get it in their home country, it can help to contact a contracted pharmacy directly to discuss this with them. Maybe they are willing to give it or they know a doctor where this person can go to. 

You can find the list of pharmacies contracted with the CAK here: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15340

Q: Where can I go to for psychosocial support? A: For an overview of where to go for psychosocial support, please see HIA (Mental Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ 

In addition, you can send them this folder about mental wellbeing (it's available in multiple languages): https://www.pharos.nl/kennisbank/als-je-stress-hebt-veel-denkt-en-slecht-slaapt-engels/

**IMPORTANT** In general when somebody is saying that he feels depressed, it is important that the PA receives good help from us. It can be important that they are helped by only one person and don’t get answers from different helpdesk agents. When you have the feeling that somebody is not feeling well, inform the Team Captain or piket about it, to see if she should take over the case.

Q: Do people have the right to get legal assistance? A: Everyone has the right to legal assistance, including people without a residence permit. A Juridisch Loket (legal help desk) can help with legal issues. Some cities have legal aid centres that provide assistance. Other relief organisations, such as VluchtelingenWerk (the Dutch Refugee Council), ASKV Refugee Support and Stek, also help people without residence permits.

Q: Where can somebody go if they want to request asylum for the first time? A: People that are looking for asylum can best go to VluchtelingenWerk for advice. VluchtelingenWerk also has a 
website where people can get information or get into contact with VluchtelingenWerk: www.refugeehelp.nl

Q: Who can help someone who has been rejected for asylum, but wants to try it again? A: People that have a negative decision on their asylum, might be able to get juridical help and in some cases temporary shelter. It is good to check with them what kind of help they already received, and where they are staying. In most cities there are organizations that can give juridical advice to people that are undocumented (and received a negative decision).
You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. In case there is no specialized organization close by, then it is best to send them to VluchtelingenWerk.
