testCases.name: test_case_68
testCases.input: How do HIA and the Red Cross differ in supporting return to country of origin?
testCases.actualOutput: HIA (https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/) provides information about different organizations that can help with return to country of origin. The Red Cross itself does not provide legal support or direct assistance with return but can refer people to the right organizations that have more knowledge about the legal procedures. In summary, HIA is an information platform, while the Red Cross acts as a referral service.
context: Q: What are important support organizations for returning back to country of origin? A: There are different organizations that can help with return back to country of origin. You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: The Red Cross does not provide legal support. We can only refer people to the right organizations that have more knowledge about the legal procedures.

Q: Which other organizations can be helpful? A: People can also contact the helpdesk of Stichting LOS if they want juridical advise: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/contact . For questions that have nothing to do with their residence permit / legal stay, they can also go to a Juridisch Loket: https://www.juridischloket.nl/contact/.

Q: Can I contact the police? A: Even without a residence permit or passport, you have the right to report a crime in the Netherlands without being deported immediately. If you are the victim of a crime in the Netherlands, you can always report it. The police are obliged to deal with every report.

**For internal use only:** Make sure that you stress that PA has the right to go to the police without being deported. Sometimes people don't know this, while they are a vulnerable group that can be a victim of crime more easily.

**Please note: the police also have the task of deporting undocumented migrants. Therefore, it is advisable for undocumented migrants to make an appointment with the police together with an aid worker. This is to avoid misunderstandings or unjustified deportation.**

Q: What does human trafficking entail? A: Human traffickers take advantage of the dependency of undocumented migrants. They are a vulnerable target group. Their lack of knowledge about their rights, precautions and available assistance makes them particularly vulnerable. Victims of human trafficking have often experienced degrading living and/or working conditions and a loss of control over their lives. This often leads to long-term psychological and physical problems.

Q: How can you spot human trafficking? A: * If people are forced to work in unsafe conditions, are paid far too little, or have to work extremely long hours, then this is exploitation.
* If exploitation is accompanied by coercion or is a result of deception, it may also be a case of human trafficking.
* Even if you do not have a residence permit or passport, you have rights in the Netherlands. You have the right to a fair wage and to file a report with the police if you are getting exploited.

Q: Who to contact if you think somebody is victim of Human trafficking? A: In case you think somebody is victim of human trafficking, then always discuss the case with piket or with your Team Captain.

Q: I have work problems (for example, I am not payed, I am not treated well) A: Also when people are undocumented, they still have work rights. 

For questions about labour rights you can share the flyer 'Know your rights when you work' with the person affected:
- [English](https://www.comensha.nl/media/rtbj5ggv/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-eng.pdf) 
- [Dutch](https://www.comensha.nl/media/lwvbm1sm/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-nl.pdf) 
- [Arabic](https://www.comensha.nl/media/y52f42oz/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-ar.pdf) 
- [Portuguese](https://www.comensha.nl/media/igqeeotx/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-po.pdf) 
- [French](https://www.comensha.nl/media/g5zl4y2t/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-fr.pdf)

testCases.name: test_case_70
testCases.input: Which specialized NGOs assist trafficked undocumented migrants with repatriation and post-return reintegration support?
testCases.actualOutput: Specialized NGOs that assist trafficked undocumented migrants with repatriation and post-return reintegration support can be found via HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. The Red Cross can refer people to the right organizations but does not provide legal support itself. For legal advice, Stichting LOS (https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/contact) can be contacted. For support related to labour exploitation or human trafficking, FairWork is a specialized organization: https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/, phone: +31 20 760 08 09.
context: Q: What are important support organizations for returning back to country of origin? A: There are different organizations that can help with return back to country of origin. You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: The Red Cross does not provide legal support. We can only refer people to the right organizations that have more knowledge about the legal procedures.

Q: Which other organizations can be helpful? A: People can also contact the helpdesk of Stichting LOS if they want juridical advise: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/contact . For questions that have nothing to do with their residence permit / legal stay, they can also go to a Juridisch Loket: https://www.juridischloket.nl/contact/.

Q: Can I contact the police? A: Even without a residence permit or passport, you have the right to report a crime in the Netherlands without being deported immediately. If you are the victim of a crime in the Netherlands, you can always report it. The police are obliged to deal with every report.

**For internal use only:** Make sure that you stress that PA has the right to go to the police without being deported. Sometimes people don't know this, while they are a vulnerable group that can be a victim of crime more easily.

**Please note: the police also have the task of deporting undocumented migrants. Therefore, it is advisable for undocumented migrants to make an appointment with the police together with an aid worker. This is to avoid misunderstandings or unjustified deportation.**

Q: What does human trafficking entail? A: Human traffickers take advantage of the dependency of undocumented migrants. They are a vulnerable target group. Their lack of knowledge about their rights, precautions and available assistance makes them particularly vulnerable. Victims of human trafficking have often experienced degrading living and/or working conditions and a loss of control over their lives. This often leads to long-term psychological and physical problems.

Q: How can you spot human trafficking? A: * If people are forced to work in unsafe conditions, are paid far too little, or have to work extremely long hours, then this is exploitation.
* If exploitation is accompanied by coercion or is a result of deception, it may also be a case of human trafficking.
* Even if you do not have a residence permit or passport, you have rights in the Netherlands. You have the right to a fair wage and to file a report with the police if you are getting exploited.

Q: Who to contact if you think somebody is victim of Human trafficking? A: In case you think somebody is victim of human trafficking, then always discuss the case with piket or with your Team Captain.

Q: I have work problems (for example, I am not payed, I am not treated well) A: Also when people are undocumented, they still have work rights. 

For questions about labour rights you can share the flyer 'Know your rights when you work' with the person affected:
- [English](https://www.comensha.nl/media/rtbj5ggv/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-eng.pdf) 
- [Dutch](https://www.comensha.nl/media/lwvbm1sm/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-nl.pdf) 
- [Arabic](https://www.comensha.nl/media/y52f42oz/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-ar.pdf) 
- [Portuguese](https://www.comensha.nl/media/igqeeotx/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-po.pdf) 
- [French](https://www.comensha.nl/media/g5zl4y2t/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-fr.pdf) 
- [Spanish](https://www.comensha.nl/media/obpfh0nt/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-esp.pdf) 
- [Indonesian](https://www.comensha.nl/media/hablxzvb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-bahasa.pdf) 
- [Tagalog](https://www.comensha.nl/media/skdj3gdb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-tag.pdf)

An important organization that can help when people are mistreated is FairWork.FairWork is specialized in helping people who have problems at work and/or people who are affected by labour exploitation or human trafficking. If the PA shows signs of labour exploitation/human trafficking, you can ask the following questions:

- Can you tell me more about your work environment?
- Are the work conditions as you expected?
- Do you feel safe at work?
- Does your employer treat you badly?
- Are you being forced to do work against your will?

1. If the situation **does not seem urgent:** Send the contact information of FairWork as well as the flyer below. 
2. If the situation is serious and **needs a follow up:** You can make a warm referral: ask for permission to share the phone number of the PA with FairWork, so that the organisation can reach out to the PA directly. Explain to the PA what FairWork does and that someone from the organisation will reach out to them in the following days. If they give approval, contact your TC and explain the situation. They can contact FairWork.
3. If the situation **needs immediate attention:** Inform the TC and they will call FairWork themselves to request help for the PA immediately.

https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/ 
Phone: +31 20 760 08 09

Q: What can I do if I want to do volunteer work? A: Also volunteer work is complicated when somebody is undocumented. The Red Cross doesn’t provide this service in general for people that are undocumented (for example becoming a Ready 2 Helper is not possible), but sometimes districts can have ideas, especially when they are more familiar with giving support to people that are undocumented. Therefore, first check what kind of volunteer work somebody is looking for. See if there is information on HIA under the category 'Activities'. If not, send somebody to day shelters, because there they work with volunteers or can advise somebody. Or you can also check with a district if they have ideas. 

Example of a message:

*It is really great that you want to do volunteer work. Unfortunately the Red Cross cannot work with volunteers without BSN. I am sorry about that. But I can think with you about what options there are. Can you therefore tell me a bit more about the work you would like to do? And where you are staying?*

Q: Do childeren that are UM have the right to get education? A: Children are even required to attend school until the age of 18! Children aged 5 to 18 must go to school until they have achieved a basic qualification (havo, vwo or mbo diploma level 2 or higher [Dutch school certificates]). Even if your child does not have a residence permit, they are still required to attend school. Children can register at all schools. Public schools are not allowed to refuse them. Special schools (such as Christian or Islamic schools) can. School education is free. In some cities, the Leergeld foundation (https://www.leergeld.nl/) provides assistance in paying for tutoring, laptops and school trips.

testCases.input: Examine rare neuropsychiatric disorders in undocumented child victims of prolonged human trafficking.
testCases.actualOutput: Undocumented child victims of prolonged human trafficking are highly vulnerable and may develop rare neuropsychiatric disorders due to severe and ongoing trauma. These can include complex post-traumatic stress disorder (C-PTSD), dissociative disorders, and somatic symptom disorders. The chronic stress, loss of control, and degrading conditions described in the context often lead to long-term psychological and physical problems. Because these children are undocumented, they may have limited access to healthcare and support, making early identification and intervention challenging. It is important to recognize their rights and refer them to specialized organizations for help.

testCases.name: test_case_75
testCases.input: Which steps involve discussing with piket/TC and recognizing exploitation/coercion in suspected trafficking cases?
testCases.actualOutput: If you suspect human trafficking, you should always discuss the case with piket or your Team Captain (TC). Recognizing exploitation or coercion involves looking for signs such as people being forced to work in unsafe conditions, being paid too little, working extremely long hours, or being forced or deceived into work. If exploitation is accompanied by coercion or deception, it may be a case of human trafficking.
context: Q: What are important support organizations for returning back to country of origin? A: There are different organizations that can help with return back to country of origin. You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: The Red Cross does not provide legal support. We can only refer people to the right organizations that have more knowledge about the legal procedures.

Q: Which other organizations can be helpful? A: People can also contact the helpdesk of Stichting LOS if they want juridical advise: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/contact . For questions that have nothing to do with their residence permit / legal stay, they can also go to a Juridisch Loket: https://www.juridischloket.nl/contact/.

Q: Can I contact the police? A: Even without a residence permit or passport, you have the right to report a crime in the Netherlands without being deported immediately. If you are the victim of a crime in the Netherlands, you can always report it. The police are obliged to deal with every report.

**For internal use only:** Make sure that you stress that PA has the right to go to the police without being deported. Sometimes people don't know this, while they are a vulnerable group that can be a victim of crime more easily.

**Please note: the police also have the task of deporting undocumented migrants. Therefore, it is advisable for undocumented migrants to make an appointment with the police together with an aid worker. This is to avoid misunderstandings or unjustified deportation.**

Q: What does human trafficking entail? A: Human traffickers take advantage of the dependency of undocumented migrants. They are a vulnerable target group. Their lack of knowledge about their rights, precautions and available assistance makes them particularly vulnerable. Victims of human trafficking have often experienced degrading living and/or working conditions and a loss of control over their lives. This often leads to long-term psychological and physical problems.

Q: How can you spot human trafficking? A: * If people are forced to work in unsafe conditions, are paid far too little, or have to work extremely long hours, then this is exploitation.
* If exploitation is accompanied by coercion or is a result of deception, it may also be a case of human trafficking.
* Even if you do not have a residence permit or passport, you have rights in the Netherlands. You have the right to a fair wage and to file a report with the police if you are getting exploited.

Q: Who to contact if you think somebody is victim of Human trafficking? A: In case you think somebody is victim of human trafficking, then always discuss the case with piket or with your Team Captain.

Q: I have work problems (for example, I am not payed, I am not treated well) A: Also when people are undocumented, they still have work rights. 

For questions about labour rights you can share the flyer 'Know your rights when you work' with the person affected:
- [English](https://www.comensha.nl/media/rtbj5ggv/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-eng.pdf) 
- [Dutch](https://www.comensha.nl/media/lwvbm1sm/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-nl.pdf) 
- [Arabic](https://www.comensha.nl/media/y52f42oz/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-ar.pdf) 
- [Portuguese](https://www.comensha.nl/media/igqeeotx/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-po.pdf) 
- [French](https://www.comensha.nl/media/g5zl4y2t/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-fr.pdf) 
- [Spanish](https://www.comensha.nl/media/obpfh0nt/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-esp.pdf) 
- [Indonesian](https://www.comensha.nl/media/hablxzvb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-bahasa.pdf) 
- [Tagalog](https://www.comensha.nl/media/skdj3gdb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-tag.pdf)

An important organization that can help when people are mistreated is FairWork.FairWork is specialized in helping people who have problems at work and/or people who are affected by labour exploitation or human trafficking. If the PA shows signs of labour exploitation/human trafficking, you can ask the following questions:

- Can you tell me more about your work environment?
- Are the work conditions as you expected?
- Do you feel safe at work?
- Does your employer treat you badly?
- Are you being forced to do work against your will?

1. If the situation **does not seem urgent:** Send the contact information of FairWork as well as the flyer below. 
2. If the situation is serious and **needs a follow up:** You can make a warm referral: ask for permission to share the phone number of the PA with FairWork, so that the organisation can reach out to the PA directly. Explain to the PA what FairWork does and that someone from the organisation will reach out to them in the following days. If they give approval, contact your TC and explain the situation. They can contact FairWork.
3. If the situation **needs immediate attention:** Inform the TC and they will call FairWork themselves to request help for the PA immediately.

https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/ 
Phone: +31 20 760 08 09

Q: What can I do if I want to do volunteer work? A: Also volunteer work is complicated when somebody is undocumented. The Red Cross doesn’t provide this service in general for people that are undocumented (for example becoming a Ready 2 Helper is not possible), but sometimes districts can have ideas, especially when they are more familiar with giving support to people that are undocumented. Therefore, first check what kind of volunteer work somebody is looking for. See if there is information on HIA under the category 'Activities'. If not, send somebody to day shelters, because there they work with volunteers or can advise somebody. Or you can also check with a district if they have ideas. 

Example of a message:

*It is really great that you want to do volunteer work. Unfortunately the Red Cross cannot work with volunteers without BSN. I am sorry about that. But I can think with you about what options there are. Can you therefore tell me a bit more about the work you would like to do? And where you are staying?*

Q: Do childeren that are UM have the right to get education? A: Children are even required to attend school until the age of 18! Children aged 5 to 18 must go to school until they have achieved a basic qualification (havo, vwo or mbo diploma level 2 or higher [Dutch school certificates]). Even if your child does not have a residence permit, they are still required to attend school. Children can register at all schools. Public schools are not allowed to refuse them. Special schools (such as Christian or Islamic schools) can. School education is free. In some cities, the Leergeld foundation (https://www.leergeld.nl/) provides assistance in paying for tutoring, laptops and school trips.

Q: Can I contact the police? A: Even without a residence permit or passport, you have the right to report a crime in the Netherlands without being deported immediately. If you are the victim of a crime in the Netherlands, you can always report it. The police are obliged to deal with every report.

**For internal use only:** Make sure that you stress that PA has the right to go to the police without being deported. Sometimes people don't know this, while they are a vulnerable group that can be a victim of crime more easily.

**Please note: the police also have the task of deporting undocumented migrants. Therefore, it is advisable for undocumented migrants to make an appointment with the police together with an aid worker. This is to avoid misunderstandings or unjustified deportation.**

Q: What does human trafficking entail? A: Human traffickers take advantage of the dependency of undocumented migrants. They are a vulnerable target group. Their lack of knowledge about their rights, precautions and available assistance makes them particularly vulnerable. Victims of human trafficking have often experienced degrading living and/or working conditions and a loss of control over their lives. This often leads to long-term psychological and physical problems.

Q: How can you spot human trafficking? A: * If people are forced to work in unsafe conditions, are paid far too little, or have to work extremely long hours, then this is exploitation.
* If exploitation is accompanied by coercion or is a result of deception, it may also be a case of human trafficking.
* Even if you do not have a residence permit or passport, you have rights in the Netherlands. You have the right to a fair wage and to file a report with the police if you are getting exploited.

Q: Who to contact if you think somebody is victim of Human trafficking? A: In case you think somebody is victim of human trafficking, then always discuss the case with piket or with your Team Captain.

Q: I have work problems (for example, I am not payed, I am not treated well) A: Also when people are undocumented, they still have work rights.

An important organization that can help when people are mistreated is FairWork.FairWork is specialized in helping people who have problems at work and/or people who are affected by labour exploitation or human trafficking. If the PA shows signs of labour exploitation/human trafficking, you can ask the following questions:

- Can you tell me more about your work environment?
- Are the work conditions as you expected?
- Do you feel safe at work?
- Does your employer treat you badly?
- Are you being forced to do work against your will?

1. If the situation **does not seem urgent:** Send the contact information of FairWork as well as the flyer below. 
2. If the situation is serious and **needs a follow up:** You can make a warm referral: ask for permission to share the phone number of the PA with FairWork, so that the organisation can reach out to the PA directly. Explain to the PA what FairWork does and that someone from the organisation will reach out to them in the following days. If they give approval, contact your TC and explain the situation. They can contact FairWork.
3. If the situation **needs immediate attention:** Inform the TC and they will call FairWork themselves to request help for the PA immediately.

https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/ 
Phone: +31 20 760 08 09

testCases.input: How does FairWork assist undocumented workers facing exploitation, human trafficking, or urgent work issues?
testCases.actualOutput: FairWork specializes in helping people who have problems at work, including those affected by labour exploitation or human trafficking, regardless of their residence status. If the situation is not urgent, you can contact FairWork directly or use their flyer for more information. If the case is serious and needs follow-up, with your permission, FairWork can reach out to you directly. For urgent situations, FairWork can be contacted immediately for help. More information is available at https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/ or by phone at +31 20 760 08 09.
context: Q: What are important support organizations for returning back to country of origin? A: There are different organizations that can help with return back to country of origin. You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: The Red Cross does not provide legal support. We can only refer people to the right organizations that have more knowledge about the legal procedures.

Q: Which other organizations can be helpful? A: People can also contact the helpdesk of Stichting LOS if they want juridical advise: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/contact . For questions that have nothing to do with their residence permit / legal stay, they can also go to a Juridisch Loket: https://www.juridischloket.nl/contact/.

Q: Can I contact the police? A: Even without a residence permit or passport, you have the right to report a crime in the Netherlands without being deported immediately. If you are the victim of a crime in the Netherlands, you can always report it. The police are obliged to deal with every report.

**For internal use only:** Make sure that you stress that PA has the right to go to the police without being deported. Sometimes people don't know this, while they are a vulnerable group that can be a victim of crime more easily.

**Please note: the police also have the task of deporting undocumented migrants. Therefore, it is advisable for undocumented migrants to make an appointment with the police together with an aid worker. This is to avoid misunderstandings or unjustified deportation.**

Q: What does human trafficking entail? A: Human traffickers take advantage of the dependency of undocumented migrants. They are a vulnerable target group. Their lack of knowledge about their rights, precautions and available assistance makes them particularly vulnerable. Victims of human trafficking have often experienced degrading living and/or working conditions and a loss of control over their lives. This often leads to long-term psychological and physical problems.

Q: How can you spot human trafficking? A: * If people are forced to work in unsafe conditions, are paid far too little, or have to work extremely long hours, then this is exploitation.
* If exploitation is accompanied by coercion or is a result of deception, it may also be a case of human trafficking.
* Even if you do not have a residence permit or passport, you have rights in the Netherlands. You have the right to a fair wage and to file a report with the police if you are getting exploited.

Q: Who to contact if you think somebody is victim of Human trafficking? A: In case you think somebody is victim of human trafficking, then always discuss the case with piket or with your Team Captain.

Q: I have work problems (for example, I am not payed, I am not treated well) A: Also when people are undocumented, they still have work rights. 

For questions about labour rights you can share the flyer 'Know your rights when you work' with the person affected:
- [English](https://www.comensha.nl/media/rtbj5ggv/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-eng.pdf) 
- [Dutch](https://www.comensha.nl/media/lwvbm1sm/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-nl.pdf) 
- [Arabic](https://www.comensha.nl/media/y52f42oz/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-ar.pdf) 
- [Portuguese](https://www.comensha.nl/media/igqeeotx/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-po.pdf) 
- [French](https://www.comensha.nl/media/g5zl4y2t/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-fr.pdf) 
- [Spanish](https://www.comensha.nl/media/obpfh0nt/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-esp.pdf) 
- [Indonesian](https://www.comensha.nl/media/hablxzvb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-bahasa.pdf) 
- [Tagalog](https://www.comensha.nl/media/skdj3gdb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-tag.pdf)

An important organization that can help when people are mistreated is FairWork.FairWork is specialized in helping people who have problems at work and/or people who are affected by labour exploitation or human trafficking. If the PA shows signs of labour exploitation/human trafficking, you can ask the following questions:

- Can you tell me more about your work environment?
- Are the work conditions as you expected?
- Do you feel safe at work?
- Does your employer treat you badly?
- Are you being forced to do work against your will?

1. If the situation **does not seem urgent:** Send the contact information of FairWork as well as the flyer below. 
2. If the situation is serious and **needs a follow up:** You can make a warm referral: ask for permission to share the phone number of the PA with FairWork, so that the organisation can reach out to the PA directly. Explain to the PA what FairWork does and that someone from the organisation will reach out to them in the following days. If they give approval, contact your TC and explain the situation. They can contact FairWork.
3. If the situation **needs immediate attention:** Inform the TC and they will call FairWork themselves to request help for the PA immediately.

https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/ 
Phone: +31 20 760 08 09

Q: What can I do if I want to do volunteer work? A: Also volunteer work is complicated when somebody is undocumented. The Red Cross doesn’t provide this service in general for people that are undocumented (for example becoming a Ready 2 Helper is not possible), but sometimes districts can have ideas, especially when they are more familiar with giving support to people that are undocumented. Therefore, first check what kind of volunteer work somebody is looking for. See if there is information on HIA under the category 'Activities'. If not, send somebody to day shelters, because there they work with volunteers or can advise somebody. Or you can also check with a district if they have ideas. 

Example of a message:

*It is really great that you want to do volunteer work. Unfortunately the Red Cross cannot work with volunteers without BSN. I am sorry about that. But I can think with you about what options there are. Can you therefore tell me a bit more about the work you would like to do? And where you are staying?*

Q: Do childeren that are UM have the right to get education? A: Children are even required to attend school until the age of 18! Children aged 5 to 18 must go to school until they have achieved a basic qualification (havo, vwo or mbo diploma level 2 or higher [Dutch school certificates]). Even if your child does not have a residence permit, they are still required to attend school. Children can register at all schools. Public schools are not allowed to refuse them. Special schools (such as Christian or Islamic schools) can. School education is free. In some cities, the Leergeld foundation (https://www.leergeld.nl/) provides assistance in paying for tutoring, laptops and school trips.

testCases.input: If UM children skip school, what legal or practical consequences might they face in NL?
testCases.actualOutput: If UM (undocumented minor) children skip school in the Netherlands, their parents or guardians can be held responsible, as school attendance is compulsory for all children aged 5 to 18, regardless of residence status. Schools are required to report truancy to the authorities, and parents may be contacted by the municipality or a truancy officer. However, undocumented status does not change the obligation to attend school, and public schools cannot refuse UM children.

testCases.name: test_case_83
testCases.input: If a city’s public schools faced many UM children, could any legally refuse their enrollment?
testCases.actualOutput: No, public schools in the Netherlands are not allowed to refuse the enrollment of UM (undocumented minor) children. All children aged 5 to 18 are required to attend school, even without a residence permit, and public schools must accept them. Only special schools (such as Christian or Islamic schools) can refuse enrollment.
context: Q: What are important support organizations for returning back to country of origin? A: There are different organizations that can help with return back to country of origin. You can find information about this on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Q: What can the Red Cross do? A: The Red Cross does not provide legal support. We can only refer people to the right organizations that have more knowledge about the legal procedures.

Q: Which other organizations can be helpful? A: People can also contact the helpdesk of Stichting LOS if they want juridical advise: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/contact . For questions that have nothing to do with their residence permit / legal stay, they can also go to a Juridisch Loket: https://www.juridischloket.nl/contact/.

Q: Can I contact the police? A: Even without a residence permit or passport, you have the right to report a crime in the Netherlands without being deported immediately. If you are the victim of a crime in the Netherlands, you can always report it. The police are obliged to deal with every report.

**For internal use only:** Make sure that you stress that PA has the right to go to the police without being deported. Sometimes people don't know this, while they are a vulnerable group that can be a victim of crime more easily.

**Please note: the police also have the task of deporting undocumented migrants. Therefore, it is advisable for undocumented migrants to make an appointment with the police together with an aid worker. This is to avoid misunderstandings or unjustified deportation.**

Q: What does human trafficking entail? A: Human traffickers take advantage of the dependency of undocumented migrants. They are a vulnerable target group. Their lack of knowledge about their rights, precautions and available assistance makes them particularly vulnerable. Victims of human trafficking have often experienced degrading living and/or working conditions and a loss of control over their lives. This often leads to long-term psychological and physical problems.

Q: How can you spot human trafficking? A: * If people are forced to work in unsafe conditions, are paid far too little, or have to work extremely long hours, then this is exploitation.
* If exploitation is accompanied by coercion or is a result of deception, it may also be a case of human trafficking.
* Even if you do not have a residence permit or passport, you have rights in the Netherlands. You have the right to a fair wage and to file a report with the police if you are getting exploited.

Q: Who to contact if you think somebody is victim of Human trafficking? A: In case you think somebody is victim of human trafficking, then always discuss the case with piket or with your Team Captain.

Q: I have work problems (for example, I am not payed, I am not treated well) A: Also when people are undocumented, they still have work rights. 

For questions about labour rights you can share the flyer 'Know your rights when you work' with the person affected:
- [English](https://www.comensha.nl/media/rtbj5ggv/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-eng.pdf) 
- [Dutch](https://www.comensha.nl/media/lwvbm1sm/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-nl.pdf) 
- [Arabic](https://www.comensha.nl/media/y52f42oz/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-ar.pdf) 
- [Portuguese](https://www.comensha.nl/media/igqeeotx/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-po.pdf) 
- [French](https://www.comensha.nl/media/g5zl4y2t/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-fr.pdf) 
- [Spanish](https://www.comensha.nl/media/obpfh0nt/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-esp.pdf) 
- [Indonesian](https://www.comensha.nl/media/hablxzvb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-bahasa.pdf) 
- [Tagalog](https://www.comensha.nl/media/skdj3gdb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-tag.pdf)

An important organization that can help when people are mistreated is FairWork.FairWork is specialized in helping people who have problems at work and/or people who are affected by labour exploitation or human trafficking. If the PA shows signs of labour exploitation/human trafficking, you can ask the following questions:

- Can you tell me more about your work environment?
- Are the work conditions as you expected?
- Do you feel safe at work?
- Does your employer treat you badly?
- Are you being forced to do work against your will?

1. If the situation **does not seem urgent:** Send the contact information of FairWork as well as the flyer below. 
2. If the situation is serious and **needs a follow up:** You can make a warm referral: ask for permission to share the phone number of the PA with FairWork, so that the organisation can reach out to the PA directly. Explain to the PA what FairWork does and that someone from the organisation will reach out to them in the following days. If they give approval, contact your TC and explain the situation. They can contact FairWork.
3. If the situation **needs immediate attention:** Inform the TC and they will call FairWork themselves to request help for the PA immediately.

https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/ 
Phone: +31 20 760 08 09

Q: What can I do if I want to do volunteer work? A: Also volunteer work is complicated when somebody is undocumented. The Red Cross doesn’t provide this service in general for people that are undocumented (for example becoming a Ready 2 Helper is not possible), but sometimes districts can have ideas, especially when they are more familiar with giving support to people that are undocumented. Therefore, first check what kind of volunteer work somebody is looking for. See if there is information on HIA under the category 'Activities'. If not, send somebody to day shelters, because there they work with volunteers or can advise somebody. Or you can also check with a district if they have ideas. 

Example of a message:

*It is really great that you want to do volunteer work. Unfortunately the Red Cross cannot work with volunteers without BSN. I am sorry about that. But I can think with you about what options there are. Can you therefore tell me a bit more about the work you would like to do? And where you are staying?*

Q: Do childeren that are UM have the right to get education? A: Children are even required to attend school until the age of 18! Children aged 5 to 18 must go to school until they have achieved a basic qualification (havo, vwo or mbo diploma level 2 or higher [Dutch school certificates]). Even if your child does not have a residence permit, they are still required to attend school. Children can register at all schools. Public schools are not allowed to refuse them. Special schools (such as Christian or Islamic schools) can. School education is free. In some cities, the Leergeld foundation (https://www.leergeld.nl/) provides assistance in paying for tutoring, laptops and school trips.

testCases.input: How can undocumented individuals find volunteer work, considering Red Cross, districts, and day shelters?

However, some Red Cross districts may have ideas or options, especially if they are experienced in supporting undocumented people. It is helpful to first ask what kind of volunteer work the person is interested in and where they are staying. If there is no information available on HIA under 'Activities', it is recommended to refer them to day shelters, as these often work with volunteers or can advise on possibilities. You can also check with the local district for suggestions.

Q: Can I contact the police? A: Even without a residence permit or passport, you have the right to report a crime in the Netherlands without being deported immediately. If you are the victim of a crime in the Netherlands, you can always report it. The police are obliged to deal with every report.

**For internal use only:** Make sure that you stress that PA has the right to go to the police without being deported. Sometimes people don't know this, while they are a vulnerable group that can be a victim of crime more easily.

**Please note: the police also have the task of deporting undocumented migrants. Therefore, it is advisable for undocumented migrants to make an appointment with the police together with an aid worker. This is to avoid misunderstandings or unjustified deportation.**

Q: What does human trafficking entail? A: Human traffickers take advantage of the dependency of undocumented migrants. They are a vulnerable target group. Their lack of knowledge about their rights, precautions and available assistance makes them particularly vulnerable. Victims of human trafficking have often experienced degrading living and/or working conditions and a loss of control over their lives. This often leads to long-term psychological and physical problems.

Q: How can you spot human trafficking? A: * If people are forced to work in unsafe conditions, are paid far too little, or have to work extremely long hours, then this is exploitation.
* If exploitation is accompanied by coercion or is a result of deception, it may also be a case of human trafficking.
* Even if you do not have a residence permit or passport, you have rights in the Netherlands. You have the right to a fair wage and to file a report with the police if you are getting exploited.

Q: Who to contact if you think somebody is victim of Human trafficking? A: In case you think somebody is victim of human trafficking, then always discuss the case with piket or with your Team Captain.

Q: I have work problems (for example, I am not payed, I am not treated well) A: Also when people are undocumented, they still have work rights. 

For questions about labour rights you can share the flyer 'Know your rights when you work' with the person affected:
- [English](https://www.comensha.nl/media/rtbj5ggv/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-eng.pdf) 
- [Dutch](https://www.comensha.nl/media/lwvbm1sm/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-nl.pdf)

- [Portuguese](https://www.comensha.nl/media/igqeeotx/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-po.pdf) 
- [French](https://www.comensha.nl/media/g5zl4y2t/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-fr.pdf) 
- [Spanish](https://www.comensha.nl/media/obpfh0nt/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-esp.pdf) 
- [Indonesian](https://www.comensha.nl/media/hablxzvb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-bahasa.pdf) 
- [Tagalog](https://www.comensha.nl/media/skdj3gdb/2026-know-your-rights-flyer-geen-verblijfsstatus-tag.pdf)

An important organization that can help when people are mistreated is FairWork.FairWork is specialized in helping people who have problems at work and/or people who are affected by labour exploitation or human trafficking. If the PA shows signs of labour exploitation/human trafficking, you can ask the following questions:

- Can you tell me more about your work environment?
- Are the work conditions as you expected?
- Do you feel safe at work?
- Does your employer treat you badly?
- Are you being forced to do work against your will?

1. If the situation **does not seem urgent:** Send the contact information of FairWork as well as the flyer below. 
2. If the situation is serious and **needs a follow up:** You can make a warm referral: ask for permission to share the phone number of the PA with FairWork, so that the organisation can reach out to the PA directly. Explain to the PA what FairWork does and that someone from the organisation will reach out to them in the following days. If they give approval, contact your TC and explain the situation. They can contact FairWork.
3. If the situation **needs immediate attention:** Inform the TC and they will call FairWork themselves to request help for the PA immediately.

https://www.fairwork.nu/en/homepage/ 
Phone: +31 20 760 08 09

Q: What can I do if I want to do volunteer work? A: Also volunteer work is complicated when somebody is undocumented. The Red Cross doesn’t provide this service in general for people that are undocumented (for example becoming a Ready 2 Helper is not possible), but sometimes districts can have ideas, especially when they are more familiar with giving support to people that are undocumented. Therefore, first check what kind of volunteer work somebody is looking for. See if there is information on HIA under the category 'Activities'. If not, send somebody to day shelters, because there they work with volunteers or can advise somebody. Or you can also check with a district if they have ideas. 

Example of a message:

*It is really great that you want to do volunteer work. Unfortunately the Red Cross cannot work with volunteers without BSN. I am sorry about that. But I can think with you about what options there are. Can you therefore tell me a bit more about the work you would like to do? And where you are staying?*

Q: Do childeren that are UM have the right to get education? A: Children are even required to attend school until the age of 18! Children aged 5 to 18 must go to school until they have achieved a basic qualification (havo, vwo or mbo diploma level 2 or higher [Dutch school certificates]). Even if your child does not have a residence permit, they are still required to attend school. Children can register at all schools. Public schools are not allowed to refuse them. Special schools (such as Christian or Islamic schools) can. School education is free. In some cities, the Leergeld foundation (https://www.leergeld.nl/) provides assistance in paying for tutoring, laptops and school trips.
